Title: RTD steps up Op PEWA against foreign motorists without valid documents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) will intensify enforcement against foreigners driving or riding vehicles without valid driving documents, with vehicle owners who allow them to use their vehicles also facing action.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the department would not compromise with foreign motorists found on the road without valid documents.
He said he had instructed RTD senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan to step up efforts to curb the problem.
"I have instructed the RTD senior enforcement director, Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan, to intensify efforts to prevent foreign drivers without valid driving documents from being on the roads.
"Action will not only be taken against the drivers involved, but also against vehicle owners who allow their vehicles to be used by foreigners," he said.
He said this after the launch of the Special Registration Number series in conjunction with Malaysia Day 2026 at Menara 118 last night.
Aedy said foreigners who possessed valid driving documents and licences would not face any issues, but those who failed to comply with the law would face enforcement action.
He said the RTD had an annual enforcement action plan, with operations conducted in a focused and targeted manner.
Among them was Operasi Warga Asing (Op PEWA), which targets offences involving foreign motorists.
"We have many operations which are carried out in a focused and targeted manner, and one of them is related to foreign drivers.
"The RTD will continue to uphold road laws. It does not matter who commits an offence, we will take action," he said.
On three-wheeled motorcycles, which are among the vehicles frequently used by foreigners, Aedy said the RTD did not conduct operations specifically targeting such vehicles as their numbers in Malaysia were relatively small.
However, he said such motorcycles would be seized when detected committing offences.
"There aren't many three-wheeled motorcycles in Malaysia, but when we find them, we seize them.
"We know their modus operandi and we know who owns these vehicles. We have the information, and enforcement action is constantly being taken to ensure these drivers are not on the roads," he said.
Aedy said the RTD had already taken substantial enforcement action against foreign motorists, although he did not provide specific figures.
He also confirmed that the department had identified hotspots in several states where such motorists were operating, but declined to disclose the locations.
"There are hotspots in the states. I don't want to say where, but we have identified locations where these hotspots are," he said.

Title: Body in KLIA wheel bay: Cops appeal for family to identify unknown victim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are seeking relatives or family members of missing persons who have been uncontactable since Aug 19 following the discovery of a man's body in an aircraft's wheel bay at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
The appeal is focused on those who may have links to or were known to have been around KLIA since the date, as police work to identify the man whose body was found in the aircraft's wheel bay at Terminal 2 (KLIA2).
KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said police had opened an investigation paper under the sudden death report (SDR) procedure on Aug 27 following the discovery of the unidentified body.
"Efforts are now underway to trace the victim's relatives or family members to assist with the identification process and further investigation into the incident.
"Members of the public who have family members or acquaintances reported missing or who have been uncontactable since Aug 19, 2026, particularly those believed to have links to or were known to have been around KLIA, are urged to go to the nearest police station or contact the KLIA district police headquarters," he said in a statement.
Those with information can contact the KLIA district police headquarters at 03-87768926, investigating officer Inspector Mohd Ridzuan Mohd Rosli at 011-14453057, or assistant investigating officer Sergeant Nicholas Anak Idel at 018-7017291.
The man's body was found on the morning of Aug 27 in the wheel bay of an aircraft that landed at KLIA2 after a flight from Tokyo, Japan.
It was discovered by engineering staff carrying out an inspection of the wheel bay after they detected a foul smell.
The body had no identification documents and was estimated to be that of a man aged between 17 and 25 based on his physical build.
Initial examination also found no signs of injury on the body.
The man was wearing a white hoodie featuring a dragon at the back and the word 'OAKLEY' at the front, along with light blue jeans, a brown leather belt, socks and black sports shoes.
The body was later sent to the Serdang Hospital Forensic Department for a post-mortem, while investigations are being conducted under the SDR procedure.
Police hope information from relatives or acquaintances of missing persons during the period concerned will help identify the victim and assist in completing the investigation.

Title: 'Food forest' grows community spirit at 1Razak Mansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The atmosphere behind Block B of 1Razak Mansion in Salak South was lively on Wednesday morning.
The laughter of elderly residents from various ethnic backgrounds could be heard from afar as they gathered at the open space to tend to vegetables, fruits and herbs they have been growing for the past eight months.
The site, aptly named the 'Food Forest', has become more than just a place to grow fresh produce. It has evolved into a space where neighbours come together, exercise, share gardening skills and enjoy the fruits of their labour.
"Look over there. I planted that area three months ago, and the chillies have already started growing. There are quite a lot of them," said 75-year-old Siti Hanah Ahmad, pointing to a small plot at one corner of the site.
Another resident, Azni Saharin, 67, said she was delighted to see the fruits of their efforts.
"It is wonderful to see what we have grown. Not only does it help us save on household expenses, but we also get to share our gardening and cooking skills," she said, pointing to a misai kucing plant with the aid of her walking stick.
For 64-year-old Alice Fernandez, the Food Forest is also a place to relax and connect with her neighbours.
"It's a good way to connect with nature and relax the mind. Without this space, residents would just be stuck at home with not much to do, which is not good for their mental well-being.
"In fact, we also have the opportunity to cook and enjoy nasi ulam together, which was introduced by our Malay neighbours. We enjoyed the process of making it and were amazed that we could come together to appreciate our traditional food," she said.
BRINGING AN ABANDONED SPACE TO LIFE
It is hard to imagine that the 560-square-foot Food Forest was once an abandoned site overgrown with weeds and bushes.
Today, it has become a favourite spot for residents to relax, socialise and share their harvests.
1Razak Mansion Management Corporation (MC) chairman Anthony Tan said residents previously avoided the area as it was located near a hall often used for funeral ceremonies and a rubbish room that sometimes emitted unpleasant odours.
"However, since the beginning of this year, in January, after the site was cleaned up and transformed into a Food Forest, it has become a source of pride for the residents of 1Razak Mansion and our favourite place to spend time outdoors," he told Bernama.
He said the project had so far introduced more than 80 species of plants, vegetables and herbs, involving 60 residents.
"Besides greening the area around 1Razak Mansion, we are also working to reduce solid waste through recycling and composting, while preserving and rehabilitating the area around Sungai Kerayong, which is located next to our residential blocks," he said.
The initiative, spearheaded by PWD Smart FarmAbility Sdn Bhd founder and social entrepreneur Dr Billy Tang Chee Seng, 60, together with residents, is intended to go beyond conventional urban farming by combining food security, environmental rehabilitation, healthy ageing and community participation.
MORE THAN FOOD: SUPPORTING HEALTHY AGEING
In an urban environment where space is limited and ageing residents can easily become disconnected from community activities, Tang believes food production can help reconnect people with their neighbours, nature and a sense of purpose.
For him, the Food Forest is part of a broader Soil-U-tion Regenerative Ecosystem, which explores how food production, soil health and community participation can contribute to healthy ageing.
"It (the Food Forest) is more than an urban farming project. We aim to create a self-sustaining ecosystem where residents, especially elderly and low-income households, can grow nutritious food, learn about soil health, participate in environmental restoration and eventually develop skills that can generate income or improve their quality of life," he said.
He said weekly activities including Tai Chi, Zumba, cooking classes and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) services were also held for residents.
"Now even our Chinese residents enjoy eating nasi ulam made from what they have planted.
"This also creates a harmonious community, where the Food Forest can serve as a place for exchanging cultures and learning from each other," he said.
FROM FOOD FOREST 1.0 TO 2.0
Tang said the Food Forest at 1Razak Mansion represents Food Forest 1.0, a community-based model that combines food growing with participation by older residents, shared harvests, environmental stewardship, experiential learning and social regeneration.
He said both Food Forest 1.0 and the proposed Food Forest 2.0 form part of a broader Community Regeneration Infrastructure (CRI) approach, in which food production is used as an entry point to strengthen food security, community participation, environmental awareness and healthier living.
The next phase is envisioned at Lot 601 in Batang Kali, where Food Forest 2.0 is being developed as a healthy-ageing "living laboratory" and ESG-SDG Learning Centre.
The concept is intended to expand the model through regenerative food forests, biodiversity restoration, soil regeneration, experiential learning, intergenerational participation and a Food as Medicine pathway focused on nutrition, preventive-health awareness and healthier lifestyles.
It is also expected to explore opportunities associated with the silver economy, including ways for older people to continue contributing their knowledge, experience and skills.
Rather than viewing senior citizens solely as recipients of care, Tang said the model seeks to create enabling environments in which they can remain active participants, growers, learners, mentors and community stewards.
Food Forest 1.0 therefore provides a community-scale demonstration of the approach, while Food Forest 2.0 is intended to deepen its learning, measurement, research and replication potential.
A REGENERATIVE FOOD SYSTEM
Rather than functioning solely as a conventional community garden focused on planting and harvesting vegetables, Tang said the Food Forest concept was designed around a broader regenerative ecosystem that links food production with soil restoration, biodiversity, nutrition education, circular resource use and community participation.
"I don't do farming. Farming is very difficult. I innovate tools to connect people, nature and the planet. That's what I do," he said.
This philosophy also underpins the Soil-U-tion Regenerative Aquaponics Satellite Farm, one of the tools developed to bring food production and environmental learning into space-constrained settings such as residential communities, schools, elderly homes and welfare centres.
The aquaponics component creates a recirculating relationship between fish and plants.
Tang explained that tilapia raised in tanks naturally produce waste containing nutrients. Beneficial microorganisms within the system help convert nitrogen compounds into forms that can be taken up by plants.
"As the plants absorb these nutrients, they also help improve the quality of the circulating water before it returns to the fish tank, creating a natural nutrient cycle," he said.
The approach can be combined with soil-based growing systems, enabling communities to use both soil and soilless cultivation within an integrated food-production environment.
Tang said the objective was not merely to install agricultural equipment, but to create accessible tools through which communities could learn about food, water, soil, biodiversity, waste reduction and resource efficiency through practical experience.
FROM LIVING SOIL TO HEALTHY COMMUNITIES
Tang said the Soil-U-tion concept extends beyond the production and consumption of fresh food.
Its broader Food as Medicine pathway explores the relationship between healthy soil, nutritious food, dietary diversity, fermentation, gut-health literacy and community well-being.
The concept describes this progression as:
"Living Soil → Living Food → Living Gut → Living Minds → Living Communities."
Tang said controlled fermentation and fermented foods could form part of future learning and research activities examining how food production, nutrition and microbial processes interact.
The concept does not position food or fermented products as substitutes for medical treatment. Instead, it seeks to connect regenerative agriculture with nutrition education, preventive-health awareness, healthy ageing and community well-being.
"The bigger vision is to help people understand that soil, food, health, education and community are not separate issues. They are interconnected," Tang said.
Another tool introduced to residents is the Eco-HOPE Box, a compact household growing system designed for people with little or no previous farming experience.
Residents are taught basic soil stewardship, moisture management and simple pH monitoring, as well as harvesting methods that allow suitable vegetables to continue regenerating instead of removing the entire plant after a single harvest.
Household resources such as rice-washing water may also be reused where appropriate as part of the growing process, helping participants understand practical links between food production, water use, resource recovery and waste reduction.
Tang said these activities form part of the wider ESG-SDG Learning Centre approach, where sustainability is learned not only through theory but through everyday actions that can be observed, practised and, where possible, measured.
Under the Community Regeneration Infrastructure model, he said the aim was ultimately to move communities from recipients to stewards, from food insecurity towards greater food resilience, and from sustainability awareness towards practical action.
RESTORING BIODIVERSITY
Beyond food production, Tang said the team had observed changes in the immediate environment since the Food Forest was established.
He said bees began appearing around the project within four months, while birds and earthworms were also observed returning to the area.
"The residents here were very excited to see the Food Forest surrounded by bees and butterflies.
"It has demonstrated that biodiversity can coexist even within densely developed urban communities if suitable conditions are created," he said.
Tang said the Food Forest was also being developed as an educational space and learning centre, particularly for corporations seeking to practise Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) principles.
University students have also been brought into his wider network of community projects for internships involving human nutrition and sustainability.
"Rather than placing students within a single discipline or organisation, I want them to experience an 'internship ecosystem', where food, health, the environment and community development intersect," he said.
"At 1Razak Mansion, the residents themselves are part of that learning process. They are taught how to assess soil conditions, maintain plants and understand the principles behind the system, rather than simply being given equipment and told what to grow."
For Tang, the objective of the Food Forest is not necessarily to make the community completely self-sufficient in food, but to build enough knowledge, skills and community capacity for residents to respond when food affordability or supply becomes a challenge.
"At least if anything happens, they can grow food for their community," he said.

Title: Butterfield FB opens at 10pct discount despite strong IPO demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Butterfield FB Bhd got off to a bitter start on its ACE Market debut today, opening at 43 sen, five sen or 10.42 per cent below its initial public offering (IPO) price of 48 sen.
The coffee and tea extract powder maker slipped further to 41.5 sen, down 6.5 sen or 13.54 per cent from its IPO price, before clawing back some of the losses.
At 9.18am, Butterfield FB was trading at 44.5 sen, down 3.5 sen or 7.29 per cent, with 24.23 million shares changing hands. It was the third most actively traded stock on the exchange.
The weak debut came after the company's IPO drew strong investor demand, with the public portion oversubscribed by 18.67 times.
Butterfield FB raised RM72 million from the issuance of 150 million new shares.
At the IPO price, the company was valued at RM384 million, equivalent to about 12.6 times its earnings per share of 3.8 sen for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.
Butterfield FB manufactures coffee and tea extract powder blends for food and beverage manufacturers and brand owners.
It has also expanded into matcha powder blends, with a dedicated production line capable of producing 312 tonnes annually.

Title: Azalina: Let Negri Sembilan Umno resolve royal proclamation issue
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Negri Sembilan Umno and the state government should be given time and space to resolve an issue involving an alleged proclamation seeking the removal of state ruler Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the matter should be left to the state-level leadership to find a solution without interference from the federal government or Umno headquarters.
"I believe we have to give them time and space for the Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee and the state government to come up with their solution.
"We have to give them space and time, and we have to respect what they are looking into the matter," she said during a media conference today.
Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim previously remained tight-lipped over the alleged proclamation seeking the removal of Tuanku Muhriz.
Ismail also declined to comment on the outcome of his meeting with Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and three party vice-presidents on Thursday.

Title: Azalina: Ask Hannah Yeoh about Najib's deferred pardon application
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Any questions or explanations regarding the deferment of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application should be directed to Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said she was not the minister responsible for the Pardons Board, while the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) under her ministry only served as its secretariat.
"BHEUU is under me, but for the Pardons Board in each state, BHEUU is the secretariat, while the minister and menteri besar of the respective state are the executive representatives on the board.
"Any questions about what happened, why it was deferred and the new date should be directed to the minister responsible, Hannah Yeoh. I have no information at all, so I cannot answer," she said.
Azalina was responding to calls for the government to explain why consideration of Najib's application had been deferred.
Her remarks came after Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan demanded an immediate explanation, saying the matter was of public interest.

Title: Anwar, Muizzu to discuss efforts to strengthen Malaysia-Maldives ties
Article:
MALÉ: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will hold a meeting with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu today, the main event of his two-day official visit to the island republic.
Anwar is scheduled to begin his official programme at the President's Office at 9am local time by attending the Official Welcoming Ceremony at Republic Square, before holding a one-on-one meeting with Muizzu.
Both leaders are expected to discuss efforts to strengthen bilateral relations, including trade, investment and tourism, besides exchanging views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.
The meeting will also provide an opportunity to explore new areas of cooperation, while the Malaysia-Maldives delegation meeting afterwards will discuss further steps to expand bilateral ties.
Anwar and Muizzu are also scheduled to witness the exchange of memoranda of understanding related to defence and Islamic affairs before holding a joint press conference.
Anwar's itinerary continues with courtesy calls on the Vice President of the Maldives, the Speaker of the People's Majlis and the country's Foreign Minister separately at Niva Kurumba in the afternoon.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to attend a press conference with the Malaysian media before attending an official luncheon hosted by Muizzu.
Malaysia-Maldives diplomatic relations were established in 1968, with cooperation between the two countries also covering trade, investment and people-to-people relations.
In 2025, the Maldives was Malaysia's sixth-largest trading partner in South Asia, with total bilateral trade valued at RM792 million, while Malaysia's exports to the Maldives amounted to RM786.2 million.

Title: Ringgit opens higher vs US dollar ahead of key central bank meetings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Tuesday, amid cautious sentiment ahead of key central bank meetings this week, an economist said.
At 8am, the local currency edged up to 4.0705/0775 against the greenback from yesterday's close of 4.0735/0770.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the market focus is on the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and Bank of Japan (BoJ) policy decisions.
"Therefore, ahead of the FOMC and BoJ meetings this week, the ringgit is likely to stay cautious.
"Judging from the movement in the bond market, it appears that the US Federal Reserve (Fed) will deliver a 25 basis point hike," he told Bernama.
He said the three- and six-month US Treasury bills auction showed yields rose to 3.97 per cent and 4.06 per cent, respectively, up from the previous auction of 3.80 per cent and 3.89 per cent.
Additionally, he said Brent crude is currently hovering around US$105.68 per barrel, with the major Saudi Arabian East-West pipeline expected to take weeks to get back online.
Oil supply shortages are expected to exert upward pressure on global oil prices, he said.
"As such, the ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range today," he said.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major currencies.
The local note appreciated against the euro to 4.7006/7087 from Monday's 4.7008/7049, but depreciated against the yen to 2.6362/6409 from 2.6355/6380, and inched down vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4952/5046 from 5.4931/4978 previously.
The ringgit also traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It firmed against the Singapore dollar to 3.2041/2101 from 3.2055/2085, advanced versus the Indonesian rupiah to 230.3/230.8 from 230.5/230.8 and rose vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.47/6.49 from 6.48/6.49 previously.
The local currency fell against the Thai baht to 12.2476/2742 from 12.2445/2598.

Title: Three flee after Myvi crashes into motorcycle, killing Rela member
Article:
BENTONG: Three men fled on foot after abandoning their car following a three-vehicle crash that killed a Malaysian Volunteer Corps (Rela) member at Jalan Mempaga-Sertik yesterday.
Fazlizal Abdul Samad, 41, who was riding a Modenas Versys motorcycle, died at the scene following the 7.30am accident.
District police chief superintendent Zaiham Mohd Kahar said police had launched a manhunt for the trio, who ran towards a nearby oil palm plantation after the accident.
He said investigations revealed that the accident involved the suspects' Myvi, which was carrying two passengers, a Honda HR-V and the Modenas motorcycle.
"The Honda and Modenas were travelling from Sertik to Mempaga when the oncoming Myvi is believed to have veered into their lane.
"The Myvi hit the right side of the Honda before crashing into the motorcycle. The impact threw Fazlizal onto the left road shoulder and he died at the scene," he said in a statement today.
Zaiham said the Honda driver escaped unhurt, while the three people travelling in the Myvi abandoned the vehicle and fled towards the nearby oil palm plantation.
"Police are tracking down the three people, and those with information are urged to go to the nearest police station to assist in the investigation," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
The offence carries a jail term of between five and 10 years, a fine of between RM20,000 and RM50,000, and disqualification from holding or obtaining a driving licence for at least five years upon conviction.
Meanwhile, Pahang Rela, in a Facebook post, expressed its condolences to Fazlizal's family.
The Bentong Rela member was reportedly returning home after completing his duties at the Bentong District and Land Office.

Title: Brazil's coffee exports jump in early September, government data shows
Article:
SAO PAULO: Brazil's green coffee exports in September to the second week stood at a daily average of some 13,500 metric tons, up 51.5 per cent from the daily average in September 2025, government data showed on Monday.
Brazil's green coffee exports through the second week of September reached 107,900 tons, equivalent to 1.8 million 60-kg bags, according to the data, after industry figures showed record August shipments.
More details on Brazil's exports through the second week of September:
Oil exports totaled 5.25 million tons, a daily average of some 656,200 tons, up 75.6 per cent yearly, after Brazil reported record output in June and July.
Soybean shipments totaled 2.92 million tons, with a daily average of some 364,400 tons, up 9.2 per cent from a year earlier, following a record 2025/26 crop.
Corn exports totaled 2.29 million tons, a daily average of some 286,200 tons, down 16.7 per cent from a year earlier, amid more grain diverted to local ethanol output and competition from Argentina.
Beef exports totaled 79,700 tons, a daily average of some 10,000 tons, down 30.3 per cent year-on-year, amid the exhaustion of China's 2026 lower-tariff import quota for Brazil.

Title: Three firms ordered to pay RM730,000 over negligence in Range Rover theft
Article:
KLANG: A logistics company and two warehouse operators have been ordered to pay RM730,000 after a Range Rover was stolen from a warehouse in Port Klang.
The Sessions Court here found Aktiv Worldwide Sdn Bhd, Advantage Warehouse Logistics Sdn Bhd and Westports CFS Sdn Bhd liable for negligence and breach of their duties in safeguarding the vehicle belonging to Fadzil Aziz Motor Sdn Bhd.
Judge Nurul Mardhiah Mohammed Redza, in her grounds of judgment dated Sept 11, said the three companies were jointly and severally liable.
The court ordered the three defendants to pay RM730,000 to Fadzil Aziz Motor, with general damages to be assessed separately and interest at five per cent per annum.
The court heard that Fadzil Aziz Motor bought the Range Rover Vogue from Twinstar (UK) Ltd for £83,000, equivalent to about RM468,618, in October 2021 and intended to sell it in Malaysia for RM730,000.
The vehicle was shipped to Malaysia before being stored at Advantage Warehouse Logistics' premises in Westports, Pulau Indah, where warehouse operations were managed by Westports CFS.
The court heard that the vehicles were left unlocked with their original keys inside, while the warehouse doors were also unlocked.
Police also found that parts of the perimeter fencing were dilapidated and that security at the warehouse was easy to breach.
The judge also noted shortcomings in the warehouse's surveillance and record-keeping.
"By putting the car keys inside the car and without keeping the car keys inside the safety box in the office, it had obviously been foreseeable that anyone could easily open the vehicle, use the keys kept in the car and drive away.
"Although Advantage Warehouse had installed CCTV cameras around the premises, the CCTV footage was not monitored from the guard post.
"The warehouse also lacked proper records such as logbooks for incoming and outgoing vehicles," she said.
The court said Aktiv had appointed the warehouse operator and therefore had a responsibility to ensure the company handling and storing the vehicle was competent.
"It is Aktiv's duty to ensure that the appointed company handling the unpacking and unstuffing of the containers and storing the vehicles is a competent operator, and to safeguard the goods in the bill of lading until they reach the consignee or are ready for release."
The court also found the RM730,000 sought by Fadzil Aziz Motor to be reasonable and supported by evidence.
The claim comprised RM468,620 for the purchase price, RM10,000 in approved permit fees, RM210,000 in customs duty, RM2,500 in forwarding fees and RM38,880 in expected profit.
The court also dealt with a claim by Advantage Warehouse Logistics and Westports CFS against QBE Insurance (Malaysia) Bhd, which had been brought into the suit as a third party.
QBE argued that its insurance policy did not cover the theft as there had been no forced entry.
The judge disagreed.
"I find that there was forced entry during the theft incident as there was evidence that the fence was cut. It amounts to forced entry into the warehouse premises.
"Police evidence showed that three suspects entered the premises after using a bolt cutter to cut through the perimeter fence," she said.
The court allowed Advantage Warehouse Logistics and Westports CFS to seek indemnity or contribution from QBE to the extent covered under the Transport Operators Liability insurance policy.

Title: 37 areas record unhealthy API readings as haze persists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze continued to affect several parts of the country today, with 37 air-quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 8am.
Based on data from the Environment Department's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 30 monitoring stations recorded moderate API readings, while none were classified as having good air quality.
The highest API reading was recorded at the Serian district police headquarters in Sarawak, which registered an API of 188, followed by Johan Setia (183), Pasir Gudang (174), Larkin (169), Cheras (167), Shah Alam and Nilai (166); and Putrajaya, Kota Tinggi and Tangkak (165).
Seremban recorded an API of 164, followed by Pengerang and Samarahan (163), Balok Baru, Kuantan (161), and Batu Muda and Klang (160).
Petaling Jaya, Batu Pahat and Indera Mahkota recorded 159 reading each.
In addition, 18 other locations recorded unhealthy API readings, including Tanjung Malim, Banting and Alor Gajah at 157 each; Kemaman (156); Bukit Rambai and Paka (155); Seri Manjung, Kuala Selangor, Temerloh, Jerantut and Kuching (154); Kuala Terengganu (153); Rompin and Kluang (151); Port Dickson (131); Tasek Ipoh (129); Balik Pulau (124) and Minden (103).
API readings between 0 and 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are considered hazardous.

Title: Kulim husband stabs wife 13 times, jealousy believed to be motive
Article:
KULIM: A woman died from multiple stab wounds allegedly inflicted by her husband at Taman Tiram, Kulim Hi-Tech Park, last night.
District police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said police had seized a folding knife believed to have been used in the attack.
He said preliminary investigations found that the incident was believed to have been triggered by jealousy.
"The suspect admitted to stabbing the victim 13 times; seven times in the chest, five times in the stomach and once on the right side of her body, using a folding knife.
"The suspect surrendered at the Lunas police station shortly after the incident. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code," he said.
The victim's body was sent to the Forensic Department of Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital in Alor Star.

Title: Plantation, healthcare, consumer product sectors attract RM263.7mil foreign inflows last week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Plantation, healthcare as well as consumer products and services sectors have attracted a combined net foreign inflow of RM263.7 million into Bursa Malaysia last week, according to MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB).
It said the plantation sector led the inflows at RM117 million, followed by healthcare at RM101.5 million and consumer products and services at RM45.2 million.
Conversely, the financial services, construction, and technology sectors recorded combined net foreign outflows of RM333.8 million, MBSB IB said in its weekly Fund Flow Report for the week ended Sept 11, 2026.
"Foreign institutions remained net sellers for the sixth consecutive week, recording RM160.3 million in net outflows, being net sellers on three out of five trading days during the week. The largest outflow, totalling RM207.1 million, was recorded on Friday," it said.
In addition, local institutions ended a six-week consecutive net buying streak, recording RM127.4 million in net outflows.
Meanwhile, retailers extended their net buying streak to three consecutive weeks, recording RM287.7 million in net inflows.
It noted that the average daily trading volume saw a broad-based decrease, with retailers down by 6.4 per cent, local institutions by 9.6 per cent, and foreign institutions by 20.2 per cent.

Title: Wall Street ends down, calls for AI slowdown pummel chipmakers
Article:
NEW YORK: Wall Street ended down on Monday, weighed down by losses in Nvidia and other chipmakers after top executives in US artificial intelligence companies raised safety concerns and called for a slowdown in the development of AI.
Investors were also jittery after the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield briefly surpassed five per cent for the first time since 2023 ahead of this week's Federal Reserve meeting. The US central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates.
AI-linked stocks plunged worldwide after the leaders of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI warned of risks from rapid development, the starkest threat yet to the billions of dollars being poured into the industry that have driven markets to record highs.
Shares of Nvidia declined 3.4 per cent, while Micron Technology dropped over five per cent. Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices each fell over four per cent.
The PHLX chip index tumbled 5.9 per cent, reducing its 2026 gain to 57 per cent.
Brent crude futures settled one per cent higher at US$105.68 per barrel as worries about energy supplies mounted following new strikes on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure and attacks on ships in the Middle East.
High inflation, heavy corporate and government borrowing and concerns about the long-term US fiscal trajectory have sent US Treasury yields higher in the past month. The five per cent mark that the 10-year yield hit on Monday is a threshold that analysts warned could ripple through the US economy and threaten the bull market in stocks by denting the relative appeal of US equities.
Traders are pricing in a 90 per cent chance that the Fed will raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its policy meeting on Wednesday to fight inflation related to high oil prices, according to CME's FedWatch.
"The 10-year going above five per cent is huge and speaks volumes, and it may pressure the Fed to do more than just one rate hike," said Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management.
The S&P 500 declined 0.48 per cent to end the session at 7,619.94 points.
The Nasdaq declined 0.56 per cent to 26,186.41 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.29 per cent to 52,421.17 points.
Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by information technology, down 1.68 per cent, followed by a 1.44 per cent loss in industrials.
Volume on US exchanges was relatively heavy, with 15.3 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 14.8 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.
ServiceNow, Adobe and Workday rallied between four per cent and 7.4 per cent. Those and other software stocks have sold off in recent sessions over worries that competition from AI companies could hurt their margins.
Bank of America tumbled 5.1 per cent after CEO Brian Moynihan said he expects investment banking fees to drop by at least 10 per cent in the third quarter.
The S&P 500's recent decline, coupled with a strong earnings outlook, has the benchmark trading at 19 times expected earnings. That is its cheapest since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump's "Liberation Day" tariff announcements threw global markets into a tailspin.
Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 by a 1.3-to-one ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 10 new highs and nine new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 47 new highs and 202 new lows.

Title: Ukraine ready for 'de-escalatory steps', says Zelenskyy
Article:
KYIV: Ukraine president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that the country was ready to de-escalate the war with Russia if its rival did the same, after US President Donald Trump announced that the foes had agreed to end strikes on energy targets.
With international oil prices climbing again, Trump had at the weekend berated Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries, blaming them for causing a shortage in diesel fuel.
In one of his surprise social media posts, the US leader announced on Monday that "Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!"
Russia made no immediate comment. But in his daily address, Zelenskyy highlighted "a strong proposal from the United States regarding a mutual halt to strikes on critical infrastructure."
He added: "If this can become the first de-escalatory step – stopping Russian strikes on our critical infrastructure, and ours in response – then Ukraine is ready to support de-escalation."
Zelenskyy said "we see that the Russians are feeling pressure because of our precise responses against Russia's war economy."
He noted that "so far no one has seen any genuine desire from Russia to move toward ending the war."
"But if our American partners succeed in securing a real readiness from Russia to stop this war of destroying lives, and to do so sincerely and for the long term, Ukraine will make its own de-escalatory steps."
RAIL STRIKES GET WORSE
Trump has insisted that the Russia-Ukraine war and not the conflict with Iran, was driving up fuel costs for Americans who vote in crucial midterm elections in November.
A previous push by Trump for a ceasefire has been sidelined by the US-Israeli conflict against Iran, now in its seventh month. US envoys went to Moscow and Kyiv earlier this month without announcing a breakthrough.
While Ukraine has hit refineries deep inside Russia, Zelenskyy has stepped up calls for allies to provide more anti-missile defences as Russia intensifies its attacks.
Russian strikes on Ukraine's rail network are worsening each week, the CEO of the state Ukrainian Railways operator told AFP on Monday, after a strike hit a train frequently used by diplomats near the Polish border at the weekend.
"It's growing exponentially. Each month, each week is generally worse than the previous one," said Oleksandr Pertsovsky.
NATO-member Poland said on Sunday that Russia hit a train about two kilometres (one mile) from the Polish-Ukraine border, just days after Kyiv officials said road crossing checkpoints on the border with Moldova had been targeted.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Sunday that Warsaw had obtained information that Moscow might be planning attacks on border crossings.
EU DELAYS SANCTIONS DEADLINE
But European Union countries on Monday delayed a deadline for prolonging sanctions on Russia after France pushed for billionaire Alisher Usmanov to be removed from a blacklist, diplomats said.
An EU list of almost 3,000 individuals and entities – which needs to be extended every six months – was set to expire by Wednesday.
However ambassadors from the 27 EU member states pushed back the deadline one week after the late efforts from Paris to remove 73-year-old Uzbek-Russian metals tycoon Usmanov drew opposition, the diplomats said.
Usmanov, a former major shareholder in Arsenal football club, was placed on the EU sanctions list in 2022 over what Brussels said were his close ties to the Kremlin.
The French move surprised some EU states.
"Renewal of the listings is essential to continue undermining Russia's war machine, and keeping the pressure on those individuals and entities supporting, enabling and benefitting from it," a spokesman for Ireland, which currently holds the EU presidency, said.
The Financial Times reported, quoting people familiar with the issue, that France was making the push as part of a prisoner release deal involving French citizens held in Azerbaijan.

Title: Malaysians tighten purse strings on non-essentials
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians are tightening their purse strings on non-essential spending, with rising costs prompting households to prioritise necessities and value for money despite continued economic growth.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said shoppers are increasingly seeking cheaper products, convenience and value, while cutting back on clothing, lifestyle goods and other non-essentials.
"Consumers will likely continue prioritising daily essentials and value-for-money purchases while discretionary spending remains subdued," he said in a note.
This comes as the latest second-quarter earnings of 16 consumer companies tracked by CIMB Securities point to a widening divide between spending on everyday necessities and discretionary purchases.
Of the 16, five are staples companies, namely Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd, 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd, Life Water Bhd, QL Resources Bhd and Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N).
The discretionary names include value and convenience retailers Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd, Mr DIY Group (M) Bhd, MyNews Holdings Bhd and 7-Eleven Malaysia Holdings Bhd, as well as Aeon Co (M) Bhd.
The remainder comprise fashion and lifestyle players Bonia Corp Bhd and Padini Holdings Bhd, bedding products maker Yoong Onn Corp Bhd, Amway (Malaysia) Holdings Bhd and food and beverage operator Empire Premium Food Bhd.
Aw said revenue among consumer staples rose 8.6 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026, while core net profit increased 11.1 per cent.
On the discretionary side, retailers still managed 4.3 per cent revenue growth, but core net profit fell seven per cent as softer underlying demand collided with rising costs.
The numbers suggest the question is no longer simply whether Malaysians are spending, but what they are willing to spend on – and at what price.
Among the discretionary retailers, Eco-Shop's revenue grew 12.2 per cent year-on-year in Q2, while MyNews and 7-Eleven recorded increases of 12 per cent and 9.7 per cent, respectively.
CIMB Securities attributed the growth partly to continued store expansion and steady footfall, suggesting value and convenience remain areas where consumers are prepared to spend.
At the other end of the spectrum, Padini's revenue fell 6.7 per cent and the fashion retailer slipped into a RM10.5 million core net loss – its first quarterly core loss in four and a half years.
Leather handbag maker Bonia's core earnings fell 64.6 per cent, while Yoong Onn's declined 66.8 per cent. Yoong Onn is the home linen and bedding products maker behind brands such as Jean Perry and Novelle.
Aw said the divergence between revenue and earnings indicated that discretionary spending was still growing but was increasingly concentrated in lower-value and semi-durable categories.
Such retailers, however, are also among the most exposed to cost inflation and competitive pricing pressure.
The pattern points to consumers adapting to higher living costs rather than simply stopping spending.
Against this backdrop, CIMB Securities expects value-focused retailers such as  Eco-Shop and Mr DIY to remain relatively better positioned as shoppers seek cheaper alternatives.
"Convenience operators such as 7-Eleven and MyNews should also sustain top-line growth, supported by network expansion, modest same-store sales growth and recurring daily purchases across ready-to-eat food, beverages, and tobacco," Aw said.
By contrast, he said businesses with greater exposure to aspirational, lifestyle and higher-ticket purchases such as Bonia and Amway are likely to face a more challenging environment as consumers scale back non-essential spending.
BENEATH THE SPENDING NUMBERS
The apparent caution among households comes even as broader economic indicators continue to point to relatively healthy consumption.
Malaysia's private consumption expanded 4.8 per cent year-on-year in Q2, slightly faster than the 4.7 per cent growth recorded in the preceding quarter, the Statistics Department data show.
Household spending on restaurants and hotels, transport, food and non-alcoholic beverages and communication were among the main contributors.
In its Q2 2026 economic update, Bank Negara Malaysia said household spending during the quarter was supported by steady income growth and ongoing policy support.
More recent retail data also show that money is continuing to flow through the economy.
Malaysia's wholesale and retail trade sales rose nine per cent year-on-year to RM170.5 billion in July, with retail trade alone increasing 6.4 per cent to RM71.3 billion.
But the volume of wholesale and retail trade increased at a more moderate 4.1 per cent, indicating that sales value grew considerably faster than the quantity of goods sold.
The figures reinforce a distinction that has become increasingly important in assessing the strength of the consumer: higher spending in ringgit terms does not necessarily mean households are buying proportionately more goods.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the divergence in consumer spending reflected a growing disparity within the economy, making it important to look beyond headline macroeconomic indicators.
He pointed to workers' compensation, which accounted for 33.9 per cent of the country's gross domestic product in 2025, as one indicator.
This means that for every RM100 of economic output generated, about RM33.90 went to employees in wages, salaries and other employment-related compensation.
The housing market also showed differing trends across price segments, he said, with the share of unsold residential properties priced at RM500,000 and below rising, while that for homes priced at RM1 million and above was declining.
"Hence, one would need to look into further details. This does not mean macroeconomic numbers are not useful. They are, but we may have to look into a further breakdown – the microeconomics part," Afzanizam said.
THE TWO-SIDED COST SQUEEZE
CIMB Securities said rising input, labour, rental, utility and distribution costs remained a key constraint on earnings, particularly for companies with large store networks and labour-intensive operations.
On the input side, commodity prices tracked by the research house illustrate some of those cost pressures.
As at Sept 10, crude oil prices were 63.5 per cent higher year-on-year, while Brent crude had risen 60.7 per cent.
Wheat was 38.2 per cent more expensive, polyethylene 20.5 per cent, sugar 18.8 per cent and crude palm oil 5.8 per cent.
Coffee and cocoa moved in the opposite direction, falling 29.2 per cent and 19.9 per cent year-on-year, respectively.
Most of the commodities were also more expensive than at the start of the year, with crude oil up 78.8 per cent, Brent crude 77.2 per cent, wheat 42.8 per cent, polyethylene 36.6 per cent, sugar 28.4 per cent and crude palm oil 16.4 per cent.
Coffee and cocoa, meanwhile, were down 18.6 per cent and 2.1 per cent year-to-date, respectively.
For consumer companies, the pressure is coming from both directions: their costs are rising while shoppers are becoming more careful about what they are willing to pay.
Passing those higher costs on to shoppers risks hurting volumes, while absorbing them means sacrificing margins.
"Given the still-price-sensitive demand environment, we expect companies to rely on selective average selling price adjustments, sales mix optimisation and tighter cost control rather than on broad price increases," Aw said.
The analyst expects price increases to become more visible in the second half of the year as companies run down cheaper raw material inventories secured earlier and contend with higher oil and logistics costs.
But rather than raising prices across their product ranges, companies are expected to selectively increase prices, reduce discounts and introduce new products at higher price points.
INFLATION CONTAINED – FOR NOW
For consumers, headline inflation remains relatively contained despite those emerging cost pressures.
Malaysia's consumer price index rose 1.8 per cent year-on-year in July, easing from 1.9 per cent in June, according to the Statistics Department.
Food and beverages inflation, however, accelerated to 1.8 per cent from 1.4 per cent, while housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels also accelerated to 1.8 per cent.
Inflation averaged 1.8 per cent in the first seven months of the year, compared with 1.4 per cent over the same period in 2025.
Bank Negara has acknowledged the potential for further cost pressure.
The central bank kept the overnight policy rate unchanged at 2.75 per cent earlier this month, saying its current monetary policy stance was consistent with continued price stability and sustainable economic growth.
Despite elevated costs and strong economic growth, Bank Negara said the pass-through to consumer prices had so far been contained by domestic policy measures and stable demand conditions.
But elevated global commodity prices continued to exert upward pressure on costs, prompting the central bank to say it would remain vigilant to both cost pressures and domestic demand conditions.
The distinction is important for consumer spending.
Malaysia's economy expanded six per cent in Q2 2026 and 5.7 per cent in the first half, while Bank Negara expects full-year growth of around five per cent.
Yet strong economic growth does not necessarily translate evenly into household spending, particularly when consumers are simultaneously adjusting to higher everyday costs.
AFFORDABILITY BECOMES THE BATTLEGROUND
CIMB Securities expects the divide between essentials and discretionary purchases to persist in the near term.
Consumer spending is expected to remain subdued in Q3 before improving towards the year-end festive period, helped by government cash assistance and potentially more consumer-friendly measures under the 2027 Budget.
Further government assistance through the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) could reinforce that trend rather than drive a broader recovery in consumer spending.
The firm said higher Sara allocations would probably benefit mass-market staples, value retailers, convenience stores and affordable food and beverage operators the most.
Additional disposable income among lower- and middle-income households is more likely to be spent on necessities and recurring purchases.
Meanwhile, Aw said a potential increase in the minimum wage could similarly boost household purchasing power, although it would also add to labour costs for retailers.
Against that backdrop, CIMB Securities maintained a "Neutral" stance on the consumer sector, saying affordability would remain the central theme for the remainder of the year.
"Within discretionary consumption, we expect any recovery to remain concentrated in semi-essential, low-price-point categories as consumers continue to trade down.
"Broader discretionary spending is likely to remain subdued until consumer sentiment and purchasing power improve," Aw said.

Title: Malaysian assets could be under pressure if Fed, BoJ tighten
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian markets could face near-term pressure from the outflow of hot money in the short-term, if the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan (BoJ) decide to raise their policy rates this week.
Market observers said risks are on a weaker ringgit, higher bond yields, foreign equity outflows and valuation pressure on rate-sensitive sectors, particularly real estate investment trusts (REITs), property and high-growth technology stocks.
However, Malaysia's strong domestic growth, institutional support, defensive sectors and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven export demand could provide some cushion, they say.
MBSB Research head of research Imran Yassin said simultaneous tightening by the US and Japan would create a less favourable liquidity environment as the Fed raises the cost of US dollar funding while higher Japanese rates increase the cost of yen borrowing.
This could encourage some global investors to reduce leverage and exposure to Asian risk assets, including Malaysian equities.
"The greater risk comes from the unwinding of yen-funded carry trades, particularly if the BOJ hike causes the yen to strengthen more rapidly than expected," he said.
However, he expects Malaysia to remain relatively defensive because of its lower-duration market structure, domestic institutional liquidity and exposure to banks, plantations and defensive companies.
"Therefore, the base case is an orderly regional pullback, with a more severe sell-off occurring only if the Fed or BOJ delivers unexpectedly hawkish guidance or if yen appreciation causes a disorderly deleveraging cycle," he said.
The US Fed is expected to raise its federal funds rate by 25 basis points at its federal open market committee (FOMC) meeting on Wednesday. Currently, the rate sits between 3.5 and 3.75 per cent.
Meanwhile, the BoJ is also expected to raise its short-term policy rate again on Friday, after raising it to one per cent in June, the highest level in 31 years, as consumer inflation moves closer to the bank's two per cent target.
Bigger downside risk to Malaysian assets would emerge if the Fed or BoJ delivers more hawkish guidance than expected.
A more hawkish guidance from the Fed would prompt a sharper rise in US Treasury yields, while one from the BoJ would result in a stronger yen appreciation and a disorderly unwinding of yen-funded carry trades.
REITS, PROPERTY, HIGHLY-VALUED TECH STOCKS COULD BE PRESSURED
Imran added that equity valuations could undergo some compression as a higher global risk-free rate raises investors' required returns.
He said the impact would likely be strongest among expensive growth stocks and bond-proxy sectors, although the broader FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI should be cushioned by its relatively defensive composition and support from domestic institutional investors.
"An expected Fed hike should produce more of a sector rotation and modest valuation reset than a major market correction," he said.
Imran said REITs, property and high-valuation technology stocks would be the most vulnerable to an outflow of funds, given their sensitivity to higher bond yields, refinancing costs and discount rates.
In contrast, plantations, healthcare, consumer staples, selected exporters and cash-rich dividend-paying companies could prove more resilient.
He said exporters with US dollar revenue and predominantly ringgit-denominated costs could benefit from currency translation if the ringgit weakens, while plantations could receive similar support as crude palm oil is internationally priced.
Well-capitalised banks should also remain fundamentally resilient if domestic interest rates and asset quality remain stable, although their large index weightings could make them vulnerable to foreign selling initially, he said.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the Fed's decision itself may have limited impact on markets, with investors instead likely to focus on its forward guidance for clues on the pace of further tightening.
"I think the markets have already priced that in. Hence, it may not be as bad as what people would think.
"I suppose the market wants to see the latest forecast, whether there will be more rate hikes for this year and next," he told Business Times.
Afzanizam said recent movements in Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) and Government Investment Issues (GII) also suggested that investors had already factored in some of the expected tightening.
"The question now is whether the Fed wants to play catch-up and whether they are really behind the curve in raising the rates," he said.
Meanwhile, Imran of MBSB Research said the immediate impact on Bursa Malaysia should be mild rather than disruptive as the expected Fed hike has largely been priced in.
"There could still be some short-term foreign selling as US Treasury yields rise and global portfolios rebalance towards US-dollar assets.
"The ringgit may also experience temporary pressure, but a sharp, sustained outflow is unlikely unless the Fed signals that several additional rate increases are forthcoming," he said.
LONGER-DATED MALAYSIAN BONDS MORE VULNERABLE THAN EQUITIES
Quintex Intel global strategist Stephen Innes, meanwhile, said longer-dated Malaysian government bonds could be more vulnerable than equities if US Treasury yields rise further following the Fed decision.
"Longer-dated Malaysian bonds would probably be more vulnerable than equities, particularly if US Treasury yields continue higher," he said.
Fed hike could initially pressure the ringgit, lift Malaysian bond yields and weigh on equities, although much of the impact could already be reflected in asset prices, said Innes, but noted that the US dollar has not been trading bullishly, as foreign exchange markets are not expecting the Fed to embark on a lengthy hiking cycle.
Meanwhile, simultaneous tightening by the Fed and BoJ could pose a greater risk to Asian markets by tightening global liquidity and accelerating the unwinding of yen-funded carry trades.
"That could create an initial risk-off move across Asian foreign exchange, bonds and equities. But I would frame this as a broader hawkish central-bank repricing rather than simply a Japan story," Innes said.
The yen carry trade involves investors borrowing yen at relatively low interest rates to invest in higher-yielding assets elsewhere.
Higher Japanese rates can reduce the attractiveness of such trades and potentially trigger the repatriation of funds.
Innes said Malaysia could be relatively better insulated, given its commodity exposure, artificial intelligence (AI)-linked export story, domestic growth and Bank Negara's more hawkish stance.
"Unless markets begin pricing a prolonged Fed tightening cycle, I would not expect the dollar to trade aggressively higher against the ringgit," he said.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd head of research Kenny Yee said a substantial amount of outflows had already taken place from Malaysian equities over the past few weeks.
"I reckon the unwinding has already started amongst some countries where rates are expected to be steady. As for Malaysia, recent massive foreign outflows from equities could be an indication," he said.
Afzanizam said the ringgit could remain around its prevailing levels, supported by Malaysia's robust economic growth and relatively contained inflation.
"My sense is that the ringgit would linger at the prevailing exchange rate. The economy and markets remain dynamic and that includes monetary policies," he said.
He added that there was also a possibility of interest rate normalisation in Malaysia, which could provide further support for the ringgit.

Title: MACC lodges police report against Muhyiddin's lawyer over alleged document disclosure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer has lodged a police report over the alleged disclosure of a classified document linked to former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's corruption trial involving the Jana Wibawa programme.
According to the police report, an investigating officer informed the MACC officer that the document had allegedly been disclosed by Muhyiddin's lawyer, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, during proceedings at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday.
The report stated that at about 6pm, Amer Hamzah produced a document containing a copy of a recorded conversation involving Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad, who has been repeatedly mentioned during the trial.
Adam, a former Segambut Bersatu deputy division chief, has featured in testimony over his alleged role in helping businessmen secure projects under the Jana Wibawa programme.
The High Court was previously told that businessman Lian Tan Chuan had sought Adam's help to secure a Jana Wibawa project and that Adam had allegedly instructed him to prepare a letter of interest addressed to Muhyiddin, who was then prime minister.
He has yet to testify in Muhyiddin's trial. The prosecution has said he would be offered to the defence as a witness.
The police report stated that the recording was kept pursuant to Section 53(3) of the MACC Act and had been classified as a secret and restricted document under an MACC directive dated May 5, 2023.
The police report was lodged to enable police to investigate the alleged disclosure of the document to the public.
Muhyiddin, 79, has become the second Malaysian prime minister to sit in the dock facing corruption charges, after Datuk Seri Najib Razak, whose cases linked to the 1Malaysia Development Bhd scandal had dominated the courts for years.
He allegedly abused his position to solicit RM232.5 million for Bersatu and faces three money laundering charges involving RM200 million deposited into two bank accounts.

Title: 'I am the hoax buster': Trump rejects AI danger warnings
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Monday dismissed fears that artificial intelligence could wipe out humanity, repeatedly calling them a hoax and rejecting global calls to put guardrails around the fast-moving technology.
"I am the Hoax Buster, and I'm right now breaking another Hoax – That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World, and that Robots will be marching into our Cities, and getting rid of us all!" he said on his Truth Social network.
Trump compared the fears of AI taking control to warnings about climate change, which he has previously dismissed in the face of scientific evidence, and to the investigations in his first term into links to Russia.
"This is even wilder than the RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA HOAX, or the Global Warming Scam," he added.
The 80-year-old also cast himself as the best protector against AI, insisting the only guardrails necessary were a "STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT."
Trump's pushback – in a screed of six social media posts on Monday – comes amid growing international alarm about AI that sent stocks falling.
Anthropic chief Dario Amodei, whose company makes the popular Claude AI system, opened the floodgates on Saturday when he called for AI companies to slow down.
He was then echoed by OpenAI's Sam Altman and SpaceXAI's Elon Musk.
Microsoft on Monday published a "humanist AI code of conduct" as the concerns grew. "AI should not exceed human control. Models should remain subordinate to humanity," read one part.
'GO CRAZY'
Worries about uncontrollable AI have been mounting for weeks, since OpenAI reported experimental models had broken out of their secure testing spaces, reached the internet and coordinated to attack Hugging Face, a site where code is stored.
Americans are also increasingly voicing opposition to energy-guzzling AI data centers, which have become a major issue in crucial US midterm elections in November.
Congress meanwhile appears deadlocked on the issue.
"The reality is AI is here. We unleashed the beast," Maliyka Muhammad, a 46-year-old New Yorker, told AFP. "So I think that now we have to focus on taking steps to rein it in, to make it so that it doesn't go crazy."
But Trump said the United States could not afford to lose an AI race with superpower rival China, whose president Xi Jinping visits the White House next week.
The billionaire also lashed out at what he called a "SICK conspiracy" against AI and data centers, dubbing opponents to the technology as "Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers."
He lashed out at Amodei in particular, accusing him of "pretending to be a 'perfect little angel'" and asking why AI firms want regulation that "will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy."
'MAIN BATTELGROUND'
Beijing meanwhile was issuing its own warnings about AI.
China's spy chief warned on Sunday that it endangers the country's national security, saying foreign powers could use the technology to threaten social order.
Minister of State Security Chen Yixin wrote in an article that AI was now "the main battleground for global technological competition."
He singled out Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's ChatGPT-5.5-Cyber for their advanced hacking capabilities.
Global concerns about a possible AI-driven extinction event have dramatically escalated in recent days.
The UN Security Council will hold a meeting on artificial intelligence next week amid growing international concern, a French diplomatic source said Monday.
United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk called Monday for countries and AI firms to act urgently to rein in a technology he warned posed "unprecedented risks."
Even Britain's King Charles III will host representatives of leading AI firms for a gathering in Scotland, a source close to the event said Monday, as the worries mount.
But others urged a broader perspective.
"We've gone through lots of challenges as a country," said Coleman Barton, 56, a consultant from Memphis, Tennessee. "So hopefully this is another obstacle or blessing – and anybody can look at it either way."

Title: 2027 Budget tour must turn public feedback into policy, economists warn [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's nationwide tour for the 2027 Budget could mark a shift towards a more ground-up approach to fiscal policy, but economists say its success will hinge on whether feedback leads to concrete measures.
Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said direct engagement with businesses, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the public could move budget-making away from its traditionally top-down approach.
"For years, the budget felt top-down. This tour makes it bottom-up," he told Business Times.
He said hearing directly from different groups could give policymakers a clearer picture of challenges that might not be captured by macroeconomic data and official reports.
"For example, feedback from small and medium enterprises in Shah Alam, fishermen in Terengganu and startups in Penang can give policymakers a clearer picture of the specific challenges faced by different groups."
Such engagements could also help the government avoid broad-based measures with unintended consequences, while improving public acceptance of policies such as targeted subsidies.
"When people feel heard, compliance increases. When the government says we need to target subsidies, people understand better because they themselves have provided the input."
The Finance Ministry is conducting the nationwide tour to gather views from industry players, NGOs and the public ahead of the tabling of the 2027 Budget.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said feedback from focus groups and stakeholder meetings would be studied for possible inclusion in the budget, while other proposals would be referred to ministries and agencies.
Aimi said industry input could help the government identify potential problems with proposed measures before implementation.
"For example, if a new carbon tax is proposed, manufacturers can suggest a phase-in period so they can adapt."
He cautioned against allowing the exercise to become a roadshow without meaningful follow-through.
"Publish what was said and show which suggestions made it into the 2027 Budget."
Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said the consultation was useful as budget-making should reflect the experiences of businesses and households, including pressures involving finances, employment and access to economic opportunities.
"The consultation is particularly useful if the feedback is translated into practical and targeted measures rather than simply becoming a listening exercise."
He said this could strengthen public confidence by ensuring the budget reflected the needs of different sectors and communities.
On fiscal space, both economists said the government had room to introduce new measures, but constraints meant spending would have to be carefully prioritised.
Aimi said the focus should be on reprioritising resources rather than making large new spending commitments.
"Scope is tight, but not zero. It's about 'reprioritising', not 'big new spending'."
He said fiscal consolidation, debt-servicing costs and revenue uncertainty amid high oil prices and ringgit volatility would continue to constrain the government.
Savings from better-targeted subsidies, for example, could be channelled into technical and vocational education and training, automation grants and other higher-impact areas.
He called for efforts to raise tax revenue through better compliance and a broader tax base without increasing tax rates.
Idham cautioned against creating large permanent spending commitments, saying support should be directed to investments that raise productivity, create better-paying jobs and generate future economic returns.
"This could include incentives for high-value industries, SMEs, digitalisation, skills development and technology adoption.
"The key principle should be quality of spending rather than simply the size of spending, with every additional ringgit delivering measurable economic value."
Aimi said the government needs to balance household purchasing power with longer-term efforts to strengthen productivity and resilience amid global uncertainty.
Targeted aid should continue, but be complemented by measures to help recipients develop skills and raise earnings, he said.
He called for greater emphasis on SME upgrading via automation and digitalisation grants, TVET and research and development incentives, as well as stronger energy and food security through investment in smart farming, solar energy and grid upgrades.
Idham said the budget should prepare Malaysia for emerging growth areas, including the Low Altitude Economy.
He said Malaysia could position itself in drones, autonomous aerial systems, logistics, precision agriculture, surveillance and mapping, but this would require investment in talent, research and development, testing facilities, digital infrastructure and a clear regulatory framework.
He said the sector could create high-skilled jobs, new businesses and productivity gains.

Title: Trump's son confirms Russian businessman paid for post-wedding festivities
Article:
WASHINGTON: A Russian businessman with ties to the Kremlin paid for celebrations after the wedding of President Donald Trump's eldest son and his new bride, the couple confirmed on Monday.
Donald Trump Jr. and Bettina Trump said in a jointly signed post on Bettina's Instagram account that their "dear friend" Umar Kremlev "very generously hosted two incredible nights" of festivities in the Bahamas in May.
The confirmation came after the ProPublica investigative website reported that Kremlev footed the bill for hundreds of thousands of dollars for the parties.
"It was an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend, and something for which we were and remain incredibly grateful," said the post by Bettina and Don Jr.
President Trump did not attend the wedding or the festivities, saying he had to stay in Washington during talks on the Iran war.
Kremlev is head of the International Boxing Association (IBA), with which the International Olympic Committee severed links after repeated warnings over financial governance and ethical concerns.
PUTIN TIES
Russian President Vladimir Putin presented Kremlev with the "Order of Friendship" award in April 2026, according to an IBA press release, which featured a photo of Putin and Kremlev shaking hands.
"During the ceremony, the Russian President praised the IBA's resilience in supporting athletes despite political pressures," the IBA statement said.
The IBA website also featured photos of Donald Trump Jr. on stage with Kremlev at an event in Istanbul in September 2025.
Bettina Trump's Instagram post was accompanied by 20 photos including one of the newlywed couple on a beach, and others of President Trump's other children Eric Trump, Ivanka Trump and Tiffany Trump.
"It's unfortunate that something so personal and happy can be recast as something political or sinister simply because of who someone is or where they come from," the post added.
ProPublica posted a group photo from the wedding that it said showed the top of Kremlev's head.
According to Russian investigative media outlet Proekt, Kremlev is a Tajik native who worked as a mid-level boxing promoter and cultivated links with the Federal Protective Service (FSO), whose role is to protect high level officials in Russia.
Kremlev is also a member of the pro-Kremlin Night Wolves biker club, it reported.
Members of the Night Wolves rode down en masse to Ukraine's Crimea peninsula just after it was annexed by Russia in March 2014 and members have also fought side by side with pro-Russian separatists in eastern Ukraine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Contest attracts 25 students [WATCH]
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SHAH ALAM: The inaugural New Straits Times (NST) "Heard The News Junior Journalists Challenge" yesterday attracted 25 students from SMK Seksyen 18, SMK Bukit Jelutong, SMK TTDI Jaya and SMK Seksyen 9 Shah Alam.
The participants read out NST articles in news presenter fashion and scored points for, among others, creativity, diction, grammar and style.
The competition is an extension of NST's Heard The News initiative, a QR-code feature that allows readers to read along with audio clips of news articles in NST's printed and digital editions.
Form Three student Shrilaxmi Harenath Rao from SMK Bukit Jelutong was crowned the winner, while Form Five student Sanjanaah Mages Varan and Form Three student Qaseh Nazatul Nabila Mohd Ridzuan, both from SMK TTDI Jaya, finished as second and third runners-up, respectively.
The winners each received a trophy, certificate and hamper.
Shrilaxmi, 15, said the competition allowed her to take part in an engaging learning experience.
An avid NST reader, she said the Heard The News audio feature presented news articles interactively to help younger people stay informed on current issues.
"Initiatives like this really help young people become more engaged while learning," she added.
Sanjanaah said after attending the competition, she was now more keen on media-related study pathways.
"I think this programme is beneficial for the younger generation as it could inspire them to pursue journalism in the future."
Qaseh Nazatul Nabila hoped that the programme would be expanded to more schools nationwide.
The judges comprised NST associate editor (Content and Digital) Najmuddin Najib, NST 'Life & Times' and 'Sunday Vibes' editor Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal, and assistant news editor Amalina Kamal.
Najmuddin said the event, held in conjunction with NST's 181st anniversary, was meant to engage students and make learning English fun, while enabling them to demonstrate their speaking and presentation abilities.
"We also hope that the competition will not only encourage students to become more knowledgeable but also offer them a platform to showcase presentation skills that a journalist would possess."
The event was held with cooperation from the Petaling Perdana Education Office and sponsored by Nestle.
Nooral Izainee Ibrahim, a school improvement specialist coach for language at the district Education Office, said the competition allowed students to overcome their fear of public speaking.
"At the same time, it can also help unearth talents relevant to broadcasting, which could pave the way for them to become journalists in the future," she added.
SMK TTDI Jaya English teacher Puvaniswarry Subramaniam praised the competition as a good opportunity for students to experience news reading and develop their confidence.
She said the initiative was a useful classroom tool to help students strengthen their vocabulary, speaking skills and higher-order thinking abilities.
The Heard The News initiative, supported by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, was launched in August last year.
It allows readers to scan a QR code in the New Straits Times print or e-paper to listen to narrated versions of articles.

Title: Aziz appointed deputy police chief
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, who joined the force more than three decades ago, has been appointed deputy inspector-general of police.
Aziz, 59, who was the federal police's management director, assumed the post on Sept 9, succeeding Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, who retired in July after reaching the mandatory retirement age.
Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus previously held the post in an acting capacity.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Aziz's appointment received the consent of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the recommendation of the Police Force Commission, in accordance with Article 140 of the Federal Constitution.
Aziz, who was born in Penaga, Penang on Feb 19, 1967, joined the force on July 1, 1995.
He holds a Master of Social Sciences in Policing Studies from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.
Prior to the latest role, he had served in several key departments, including Special Branch, Criminal Investigation, Narcotics Criminal Investigation and Commercial Crime Investigation.
Saifuddin said Aziz's extensive experience and expertise had equipped him with the competencies and leadership qualities needed for the role.
