Title: Tan Chong lands Perodua EV deal
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd has signed a three-year agreement with Perodua Sales Sdn Bhd to provide coating, painting and assembly line services for the national carmaker's battery electric vehicle (BEV) project in Serendah.
Under the deal, Tan Chong's subsidiary, Tan Chong Motor Assemblies Sdn Bhd (TCMA), will provide electro-deposition coating, painting, assembly line rental, and related support.
Perodua Sales will pay TCMA service fees and rental charges.
The agreement, which took effect on June 1, has an initial three-year term, with Perodua Sales having the option to extend it for another two years.
The extension option must be exercised at least six months before the initial term expires.
Perodua Sales will be responsible for obtaining and maintaining the necessary approvals, permits and licences, and complying with laws and regulatory requirements for BEV manufacturing.
It will also be responsible for maintaining and adequately insuring its equipment for the project.
Tan Chong said the agreement would have no effect on its issued share capital.
The project is expected to contribute to Tan Chong's revenue and earnings from the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
The agreement follows a letter of intent between TCMA and Perodua Sales announced on Nov 14 last year.

Title: Mediators to hear Cambodia, Thailand maritime dispute
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
PHNOM PENH: Cambodia and Thailand will face off before international mediators here this week in a long-standing dispute over valuable maritime resources, the latest spat between the feuding neighbours.
Phnom Penh initiated a United Nations-backed conciliation process at the Permanent Court of Arbitration after Bangkok pulled out of an agreement to work towards joint offshore energy exploitation in the Gulf of Thailand.
The 2001 memorandum of understanding covers a vast and resource-rich territory of about 27,000 sq km to which both Cambodia and Thailand lay claim.
In May, Bangkok unilaterally pulled out of the framework agreement, called "MoU 44", saying "no progress had been made" in implementing it.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul denied it was linked to the simmering border conflict with its neighbour, which erupted into two rounds of clashes last year that left dozens of people dead and displaced more than a million before a truce was agreed.
Last week, Cambodia said it resorted to the conciliation process "after Thailand unilaterally terminated the agreed bilateral framework" through which the two nations had "negotiated their overlapping maritime claims for more than two decades".
In June, Prime Minister Hun Manet said the move was also to "protect Cambodia's sovereignty and maritime rights in accordance with international law".
The two countries' representatives are set to give their opening statements today before a five-member conciliation panel of international law experts at the world's oldest arbitration court's offices here.
Cambodia's Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn is expected to open the floor, followed by his Thai counterpart, Sihasak Phuangketkeow.
Both Cambodia and Thailand have welcomed the opportunity to put their points across.
"The meeting marks another important milestone in the peaceful process initiated by Cambodia to resolve the countries' maritime differences," said Cambodia's Foreign Ministry.
Phnom Penh said it hoped the process could help Cambodia and Thailand reach a "fair and lasting resolution of their maritime differences" and open a pathway to explore significant oil and gas resources.

Title: Himalayas nearing tipping point as glacier melt threatens millions: Report
Article:
HONG KONG: The Himalayas are approaching a tipping point as glaciers melt faster than a decade ago, threatening water security as the region approaches "peak water" by mid-century, according to a study released this month.
The findings come after the collapse of a Himalayan glacier in late August along the Nepal-Tibet border, which caused cascading landslides and flash floods in the valleys below. At least 1,300 people have been confirmed dead and more than 5,300 are missing across Nepal and China's Tibet region.
As glaciers retreat, they are leaving behind unstable glacial lakes held back by little more than loose rock and ice, above valleys where millions of people live, the study found.
The study was produced by Systemiq, a sustainability advisory firm, together with the Integrated Mountain Initiative, the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, and India's G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment.
Himalayan glacier mass loss had accelerated in recent decades, while only 21 glaciers were currently monitored on the ground out of an estimated 40,000 glaciers across the Hindu Kush-Himalaya region, a vast mountain system spanning eight countries from Afghanistan to Myanmar, the study found.
Close to 200 glacial lakes in India had been identified as high risk, with 56 classified as "very high risk", leaving millions exposed downstream.
As the region neared "peak water", the point when river flows stop rising and start declining, it would have profound implications for water security. As the Himalayas underpinned more than 20 per cent of India's GDP, the region made up a key piece of the country's national economic infrastructure, upon which hundreds of millions of people depended.
Though making up around 18 per cent of India's land, the Himalayan region accounted for roughly 35 per cent of the country's natural disasters.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia rescuers battle turbulent seas in search for 129 people after passenger ship capsizes
Article:
JAKARTA: Hundreds of Indonesian rescuers including the coast guard and the navy raced on Monday to board a passenger ship that capsized in the Java Sea over the weekend as they searched for 129 people still missing, officials said, with the confirmed death toll at six.
The Virgo Transport 8 ship carrying 243 people went missing in bad weather early on Sunday, the rescue agency said. Authorities have since rescued 108 people from the ship, which was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.
Choppy waters with high waves and strong winds were impeding the search on Monday, said Mohammad Syafii, head of the national rescue agency.
The agency has deployed at least 622 personnel, 17 ships, five helicopters and aircraft to find the missing passengers, Syafii added. Some of the ships have arrived at the location but it was difficult for rescuers to make their way into the capsized and partially submerged ship, he said.
"We would also deploy personnel with underwater rescue skills but the current conditions do not allow us to," he said.
"While waiting for the weather conditions to improve, we are identifying more personnel with special skills," he said, adding the death toll remained at six.
In a video shared by the rescue agency, a large red-and-black ship was capsized and partially submerged in choppy blue water, with its red-painted underside visible above the surface.
Two small boats, each carrying people, were seen floating in rough waters near the capsized ship.
The location of the capsized boat is around 80 nautical miles from the command centre at Trisakti Port in Banjarmasin, another official at the rescue agency told Reuters.
"The conditions there are quite windy, making it difficult for the (rescue) vessels to dock," the official, Arianto Ardi, said.
As of Monday afternoon, none of the 129 missing people have been found, Arianto said, adding that rescuers are still unable to conduct a search for the victims due to the weather.
THREE-METRE WAVE CRASHES INTO SHIP
The weather was very poor when the incident happened, with waves as high as three metres crashing into the ship, Syafii said.
It takes around five hours to reach the location from Trisakti Port in good weather but requires up to nine hours in rough conditions.
On Sunday, Edy Prakoso, another official at the agency, said the ship leaned heavily to one side after strong waves hit its starboard side.
Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said the capsized boat had the capacity to contain 500 passengers, so it was not overloaded.
The incident took place in the Java Sea - the waters between Indonesia's four most populated islands of Java, Sumatra, Sulawesi and Borneo - has been the site of some of Indonesia's deadliest maritime disasters.
A portion of the sea - around the Masalembo islands - is often referred to as Indonesia's Bermuda Triangle, given the number of air and maritime accidents that take place there.
In 1981, the ship Tampomas II sank in the area, killing nearly 600 people by some estimates. There was also an air plane crash in the same area in 2007 that killed over 100 people.
Freddy Manuhua has been anxiously awaiting news of his brother Stefiyansah at Surabaya port since Sunday. His brother had worked as a keyboard player for the ship's entertainment show for the past two months.
He remembers taking his brother, who was very excited about his new job, to Surabaya port last Saturday before the vessel left for Banjarmasin.
"I will accept whatever happens and would be grateful if I can still see my younger brother again, no matter what condition he is in," he said.
Indonesia relies on ferries across its 17,000 islands, with sea travel cheaper and more accessible than flying, but there have been numerous accidents.
Last month, two passenger ferries caught fire in separate incidents, killing six people — five off Madura island and one on a route from the island of Bali.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK PM cancels engagements after father's death
Article:
LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has cancelled his upcoming engagements Monday and Tuesday due to the death of his father, his Downing Street office announced.
Burnham has said in interviews that his father, Roy, had Alzheimer's disease and was living in a care home. He has cited his family's experience while vowing to reform the social care system.
After taking office in July, Burnham told The Times daily that his father, a former telecoms engineer who is in his mid-80s, did not know he was prime minister, which was a "sadness."
He told podcaster Elizabeth Day that his father was unable to come and see him enter Downing Street along with his mother, but carers pointed out Burnham on television and thought he recognised him.-AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia explores UAE interest in halal logistics, jobs and waste-to-energy
Article:
KERALAM : Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim held discussions with UAE‑India Business Council, UAE Chapter (UIBC‑UC) leaders to explore cooperation in investment, logistics, employment and other sectors during his working visit here yesterday.
Among those he met were Sharaf Group vice chairman Major General Sharafuddin Sharaf and EFS Facilities Services Group co‑founder and executive vice chairman Tariq Chauhan.
Anwar said discussions with Sharafuddin included Sharaf Group's interest in leveraging Malaysia as a regional halal meat distribution hub, building on its cargo and logistics capabilities. He added Chauhan shared EFS's hiring plans and opportunities for Malaysians in facilities management.
The engagements provided avenues to expand investment, logistics, employment and business collaboration, while strengthening Malaysia's links with UAE‑based companies and the wider UAE‑India business community.
Malaysia also welcomed greater engagement with UAE and Indian businesses and pledged to facilitate partnerships creating tangible opportunities for Malaysians and local firms.
The Prime Minister also highlighted potential cooperation with BEEAH Group, which has expanded from environmental origins into energy, technology, healthcare and real estate.
The group operates a state‑of‑the‑art recycling and material recovery facility in Sharjah and is looking to develop a sustainable waste‑to‑energy facility in Malaysia.
The UIBC‑UC, established in 2023 under the Federation of UAE Chambers of Commerce & Industry, promotes trade, investment and business‑to‑business linkages between the UAE and India.
Its members are active in logistics, infrastructure, retail, healthcare, technology, clean energy and advanced manufacturing.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar defends moderate approach on Umno ties, says govt stability must come first
Article:
KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has chosen a moderate approach in handling differing views regarding the issue of cooperation with Umno within the Unity Government.
Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) Chairman, stated that the government must remain stable because any overly harsh actions concerning the issue could result in losses for the country.
“I choose a somewhat moderate path because what is important is that the government must be stable, otherwise there will be many losses for our country.
“So for me, that is what is important, and I see that, for example, is also the voice we hear including from Umno,” he said during a press conference with Malaysian media in Calicut here, before concluding his working visit to India yesterday.
Elaborating further, Anwar said various views were also voiced among political parties including PH, but such matters are normal within a coalition and should not be seen as something that could threaten government cooperation.
“We listen to everything, but to my knowledge, I don’t see any problems. There are small and normal ones. Even in a household, there are minor issues, let alone with political commanders,” he said.
The Prime Minister said this when asked to comment on his views regarding several issues raised at the 2026 Umno General Assembly (PAU) recently. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Miti to pursue wider market access for Malaysian goods in India
Article:
KERALAM, Sept 15 — The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) will follow up on efforts to widen access for Malaysian goods to the Indian market, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the matter was discussed during his meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, with several restrictions still needing to be addressed to facilitate trade between the two countries.
“We believe that some restrictions are still in place, for example airlines. We are still requesting for additional facility in some other cities,” said Anwar during a press conference with Malaysian media in Calicut here, before concluding his working visit to India yesterday.
He said the matter was also raised during his meeting with Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and Malaysia would use the appropriate channels to address the matter and further strengthen trade and investment ties with India.
“This is a concern for the request from the Keralam chief minister. I think that is reasonable, but we need to address it through the right mechanism,” said Anwar.
The Prime Minister emphasised Malaysia’s view of India as a vital economic partner, aiming to strengthen trade and investment between the two nations.
He said widening market access was important to ensure more Malaysian goods could penetrate the Indian market, thereby benefiting local industries and businesses.
Earlier, Anwar and Satheesan discussed efforts to strengthen economic cooperation and facilitate greater trade and investment between Malaysia and India’s southern state, Keralam, formerly known as Kerala.
The discussion took place during Satheesan’s courtesy call on Anwar in Calicut, held in conjunction with the Prime Minister’s working visit to India and his maiden visit to Keralam as Prime Minister.
Anwar arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the BRICS Leaders’ Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and delivered the National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth. — Bernama

Title: Woman allegedly stabbed 13 times by husband after jealous row, suspect later surrenders
Article:
KULIM,  Sept 15 — A 39-year-old woman died after allegedly being stabbed 13 times by her husband following an argument at their home in Taman Tiram near here last night.
Kulim police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said the victim, identified as S. Sila, was taken to Kulim Hospital by family members and was pronounced dead at 9.30 pm.
He said the 43-year-old unemployed suspect went to the Lunas Police Station at 8.40 pm and reported that he had stabbed his wife at their home.
“The suspect also surrendered a folding knife believed to have been used in the incident,” he said in a statement yesterday.
According to Syamsul, the incident occurred in the master bedroom of the single-storey terrace house occupied by the couple and their three-year-old child.
“Preliminary investigations found that the incident stemmed from an argument between the suspect and the victim, believed to have been triggered by jealousy.
“An inspection of the scene found traces believed to be blood on the bedsheet, pillow, headboard and several items on the bed. A total of 11 samples related to the incident were collected,” he said.
Syamsul said the suspect admitted to stabbing the victim 13 times using the folding knife.
“After the incident, the suspect bathed and collected his child from a babysitter before handing the child over to his sister at the Juru Rest and Service (R&R) area in Penang.
“The suspect also told his sister that he had stabbed his wife before proceeding to the Lunas Police Station to surrender,” he said.
He said the suspect was arrested at 9 pm yesterday, while a 20-centimetre folding knife was seized as evidence.
“The victim’s body was sent to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital in Alor Setar for a post-mortem examination, and the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar seeks closer Malaysia-Keralam ties in key sectors including digital economy, healthcare
Article:
KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for stronger cooperation between Malaysia and Keralam in key sectors, including the digital economy, healthcare, tourism and education.
He said the longstanding relationship between Malaysia and Keralam, which encompasses trade, education and cultural exchanges, provides a strong foundation for further cooperation.
Anwar said this during a meet with Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar in Calicut, here yesterday.
The Prime Minister said there was also potential to further expand tourism, business and people-to-people exchanges between Malaysia and Keralam.
“Malaysia also welcome greater collaboration in high-value sectors that could create new opportunities and bring mutual benefits to both sides,” he said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied on his working visit by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
Earlier, in a light-hearted gesture, Arlekar presented Anwar with a biography of legendary Indian playback singer Kishore Kumar, following the Prime Minister’s recent viral singing performance of a Kishore Kumar song at the BRICS gala dinner in New Delhi.
Anwar’s rendition of Kishore Kumar’s classic “Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat” went viral on social media, particularly in India, drawing positive reactions from many Indians.
The one-minute, 32-second video of Anwar performing the popular Hindi song attracted widespread attention, with some describing it as a “mic drop” moment that stole the limelight at the summit, while others called it the “sweetest part” of the gathering.
Minister for Industries and Commerce P.K Kunhalikutty and several captains of industries also joined the courtesy call.
The engagement with the Governor was part of Anwar’s programme during his visit to Keralam, following his participation in the BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
Anwar is on an official visit to India from Sept 11 to 14, at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. — Bernama

Title: Anwar calls for stronger Malaysia-India synergy in E&E and semiconductor sectors
Article:
KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for Malaysia and India to strengthen synergy in the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors to enhance their respective capabilities and benefit from each other’s strengths.
He said Malaysia was positioning itself as a key player in the E&E and semiconductor sectors in Southeast Asia, while India also possessed considerable strength in these areas.
“It is an emerging economy and is focusing more in terms of E&E and semiconductor in Southeast Asia, and energy economy we are probably about the largest now, including export to the United States.
“With the strength of the E&E, semiconductor of India, can you imagine if that synergy is fortified to enhance our capability and make sure that we benefit from one another. I think it is important,” said Anwar.
He said this in his remarks at the Hi-Tea Engagement with the Governor of Kerala, Minister for Industries & Commerce, and Prominent Indian Business Leaders in Calicut, here yesterday.
Around 30 companies from India, Malaysia and the Gulf countries participated in the engagement, representing sectors including medical and healthcare, semiconductors, construction, artificial intelligence (AI), digital technology, information technology, engineering, retail, renewable energy and transportation.
The Prime Minister said the engagement provided an opportunity to strengthen business-to-business linkages and explore greater cooperation in high-value sectors.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, noted that India was an important emerging economy and Malaysia should continue to diversify its trade and investment relationships while maintaining strong ties with existing major partners.
Modern diplomatic relations between Putrajaya and New Delhi were established in 1957, shortly after Malaysia gained independence, and India remains Malaysia’s largest trading partner in South Asia, with bilateral trade reaching US$18.55 billion (RM79.33 billion) in 2025.
Anwar also highlighted the historical links between Keralam and Southeast Asia, particularly through the Malabar Coast, which he described as an important part of the region’s cultural, religious and intellectual history.
He said Keralam’s historical connections with Southeast Asia should be fully utilised to further strengthen cooperation between Malaysia and Keralam, particularly in trade and investment.
Anwar stated that Malaysia should promote increased two-way investment, encouraging capital flows from Malaysia to Kerala, as well as from Kerala and neighbouring Indian states into Malaysia.
Also present were Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Malaysia’s Chargé d’Affaires, Deputy High Commissioner Sharifah Ezneeda Wafa, and the Consul General of Malaysia to South India K. Saravana Kumar.
Anwar then departed from Keralam for an official visit to the Maldives after completing his five-day working visit to India.
The aircraft carrying the Prime Minister departed Calicut International Airport here at 7.26 pm local time (9.56 pm Malaysian time) for Velana International Airport in Malé. — Bernama

Title: Anwar, Muizzu to discuss trade, investment and tourism in Maldives meeting
Article:
MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will hold a meeting with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu today, the main event of his two-day official visit to the island republic.
Anwar is scheduled to begin his official programme at the President’s Office at 9 am local time by attending the Official Welcoming Ceremony at Republic Square, before holding a one-on-one meeting with Muizzu.
Both leaders are expected to discuss efforts to strengthen bilateral relations, including trade, investment and tourism, besides exchanging views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.
The meeting will also provide an opportunity to explore new areas of cooperation, while the Malaysia-Maldives delegation meeting afterwards will discuss further steps to expand bilateral ties.
Anwar and Muizzu are also scheduled to witness the exchange of memorandums of understanding (MoUs) related to defence and Islamic affairs before holding a joint press conference.
Anwar’s itinerary continues with courtesy calls on the Vice President of the Maldives, the Speaker of the People’s Majlis and the country’s Foreign Minister separately at Niva Kurumba in the afternoon.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to attend a press conference with the Malaysian media before attending an official luncheon hosted by Muizzu.
Anwar is scheduled to depart for Malaysia from Velana International Airport tomorrow afternoon, concluding his official visit to the Maldives.
Malaysia-Maldives diplomatic relations were established in 1968, with cooperation between the two countries also covering trade, investment and people-to-people relations.
In 2025, the Maldives was Malaysia’s sixth-largest trading partner in South Asia, with total bilateral trade valued at RM792 million, while Malaysia’s exports to the Maldives amounted to RM786.2 million. — Bernama

Title: Air quality worsens across Malaysia: 38 stations in unhealthy bracket, Johor hardest hit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Air quality deteriorated to unhealthy levels at 38 monitoring locations across the country as of 8.45am today, according to Department of Environment (DOE) data, with Sarawak recording the worst reading in Malaysia.
IPD Serian in Sarawak posted an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 188, the highest nationwide and just shy of the 201 mark that would tip it into the “very unhealthy” category.
Close behind was Johan Setia in Selangor, at 183.
Johor had more unhealthy readings than any other state, with Pasir Gudang at 172, Larkin at 169, Tangkak at 166, Kota Tinggi at 165, Pengerang at 162, Batu Pahat at 160 and Kluang at 151.
The Klang Valley was also heavily affected. Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded 170, while Shah Alam logged 167, Putrajaya 165, Batu Muda 161, and both Petaling Jaya and Klang came in at 160. Banting, also in Selangor, registered 157.
Negeri Sembilan saw unhealthy readings in Nilai at 167 and Seremban at 164, with Port Dickson trailing further down the list at 140.
In Sarawak, Samarahan recorded 163 and Kuching 154, alongside Serian’s chart-topping figure.
Pahang logged several unhealthy readings, led by Balok Baru and Indera Mahkota in Kuantan at 161 and 160 respectively, followed by Temerloh and Jerantut at 155 each, and Rompin at 152.
Terengganu’s readings ranged from 157 in Kemaman to 153 in Kuala Terengganu, with Paka in between at 156.
Melaka recorded 157 in Alor Gajah and 155 in Bukit Rambai, while Perak’s readings spanned Tanjung Malim at 157, Seri Manjung at 154 and Tasek Ipoh at 141.
Selangor’s Kuala Selangor also featured, at 155.
The mildest readings among the unhealthy group came from the northern states. Balik Pulau in Penang stood at 131 and Minden at 111, while Sungai Petani in Kedah recorded the lowest unhealthy reading nationwide at 103.
Under the DOE’s API classification, readings between 101 and 200 fall within the “unhealthy” category.
Members of the public in the affected areas, particularly children, the elderly and those with respiratory or heart conditions, are advised to limit prolonged outdoor activity and to monitor further updates from the DOE.

Title: Anwar arrives in Maldives for two-day official visit to strengthen bilateral ties
Article:
MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived in the Maldives tonight to begin a two-day official visit aimed at further strengthening Malaysia-Maldives bilateral ties, which dates back to 1968.
The special aircraft carrying Anwar landed at Velana International Airport here at 8.12 pm local time (11.12 pm Malaysian time) with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu personally welcoming the Prime Minister.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, was accompanied by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and a Malaysian delegation.
Also present to welcome the Prime Minister were the High Commissioner of Malaysia to Sri Lanka and the Maldives, Badli Hisham Adam, Maldivian Minister of Islamic Affairs Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed, who was the minister-in-attendance, as well as senior officials from both countries.
The warm welcome reflected the close and cordial ties between the two leaders and their countries.
Upon arrival, Anwar received a guard of honour and, before proceeding to the Official Jetty, was treated to a cultural performance by school students to mark his arrival in the island republic.
Muizzu then accompanied Anwar to the Official Jetty to complete the welcome ceremony at the start of his maiden official visit to the Maldives.
Tomorrow, Anwar’s programme is scheduled to begin with an official welcome ceremony at Republic Square in Malé, followed by a four-eye meeting with Muizzu and bilateral talks involving delegations from both countries.
The two leaders are also scheduled to witness the exchange of memorandum of understanding (MoUs) in areas of defence and Islamic affairs.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to receive courtesy calls from several Maldivian ministers before attending an official luncheon hosted by Muizzu.
The Maldives is Anwar’s final destination after attending the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on Friday, followed by a visit to Keralam, the new name for Kerala, before flying to the island republic.
Maldives is one of Malaysia’s important economic partners in South Asia and was Malaysia’s sixth-largest trading partner in the region in 2025, with total bilateral trade valued at RM792 million.
Malaysia’s exports to the republic amounted to RM786.2 million that year. — Bernama

Title: PM: Decision to defer Najib’s pardon petition based on law, not personal prejudice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The decision to defer former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s petition for a royal pardon was guided strictly by the Federal Constitution, the rule of law, and official legal advice, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar stressed that his participation in the Pardons Board proceedings was bounded by statute and formal guidance provided by the Attorney-General, The Edge reported.
“A prime minister, whoever he is, must have a voice and give his views based on the law, on advice from the Attorney General and on the rules. That is what I did.
“However, we also know that this is within the discretion and authority of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong (His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia), in the Pardons Board meeting, and the King must of course take all factors into consideration,” he told a joint press conference with Malaysian media in Calicut, Kerala, prior to concluding his official visit to India on Monday.
Anwar said the question of Najib’s pardon must not be viewed through a personal lens, but evaluated against established legal benchmarks and good governance.
“For me, in carrying out this duty, we must submit to the principle of the rule of law and what has been agreed upon in the constitution.
“So, I only gave my views along those lines. I have never, for example, taken a prejudiced or hateful stance. No,” he said.
The prime minister acknowledged that political representations, including strong appeals made by Umno leaders, were considered, but maintained that he chose to fulfil his constitutional duties based on principled governance.
“I know what the easy way is and what the difficult way is, but I chose the path I believe is right, following the principles of law and what we consider important in terms of the spirit of governance and the rule of law in the country,” he said.
Last Friday, Sultan Ibrahim consented to defer Najib’s pardon petition to a subsequent meeting of the board.
The decision was disclosed in an official statement by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department following the 63rd Pardons Board Meeting for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, and Putrajaya at Istana Negara on Sept 11.
On Dec 26 last year, the High Court sentenced Najib to 15 years in prison and imposed an RM11.4 billion fine after convicting him of four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering involving RM2.3 billion misappropriated from 1MDB funds.

Title: ‘Our tebu is still sweet’: Tun Jugah’s son reflects on Sarawak, Malaysia at 63
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 15 — While history was being made in Kuching on September 16, 1963, a young Leonard Linggi Tun Jugah was several hundred kilometres away in his hometown Nanga Gaat, Kapit.
He was then on a fishing and hunting expedition in the upper reaches of the Baleh River, yet he made sure he did not miss the historic moment, following the proclamation of Malaysia through radio broadcasts and newspaper reports, and hearing the views of those around him.
“At that time, I was just finishing Form 6. I listened to the radio and read the newspapers on the historic occasion,” Tan Sri Linggi, now 86, told Bernama in an interview in conjunction with Malaysia Day, which falls on September 16.
His father, the late Tun Jugah Barieng, however, was in Kuching that day.
A prominent Iban leader back then, Jugah was present at the Central Padang (now known as Padang Merdeka) to witness the proclamation of Malaysia, alongside other state leaders, including Sarawak’s first Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Abang Openg Abang Sapiee and first chief minister Tan Sri Stephen Kalong Ningkan.
Journey towards Malaysia
Sharing his recollections of his father’s contributions to the events leading to the formation of Malaysia, Linggi — a former leader of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) and MP for Kapit between 1978 and 1986 — said although Jugah was widely known as one of the signatories to the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), his involvement in the journey had begun much earlier.
(MA63 is the founding legal document that united Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore with the existing states of the Federation of Malaya to form the new nation of Malaysia. The agreement was signed on July 9, 1963, and took effect on Sept 16 the same year. Singapore officially left Malaysia on August 9, 1965.)
Linggi said Jugah played a key role in building support for the formation of Malaysia, bringing together 51 Iban headmen in Kapit on February 15, 1962, where they reached an agreement to support the formation of Malaysia.
“My father worked very hard to make sure that Malaysia was a success,” he said.
“He assembled the Iban penghulu in Kapit and chaired that particular randau awam, or conference. During that conference, the Iban of the Rajang Valley decided to support (the formation of) Malaysia.”
He added that his father was convinced that without the conference’s support, the Cobbold Commission Report would have been different. (The Cobbold Commission was set up to assess the views of the people in Sabah and Sarawak regarding the proposed Federation of Malaysia.)
Linggi said Jugah was briefed on the Malaysia proposal by the then British governor of Sarawak, Sir Alexander Waddell.
He said Waddell had explained that Britain could no longer continue governing Sarawak as the global landscape was changing and colonialism was increasingly being challenged.
“Waddell told my father that it would be better for his people, in terms of security and economic progress, to go together with Malaya, Sabah and the others.
“My father also knew that the communist movement was on the rise at the time. Our neighbours, Indonesia and the Philippines, were not particularly friendly towards us either. He (Jugah) felt that (the proposal to form) Malaysia was worth supporting.
“That was his rationale at the time. But first, he needed to convince the Iban, and he succeeded,” he said.
Malaysia 63 years later
Reflecting on the 63 years since the formation of Malaysia, Linggi said the nation had largely realised the aspirations envisioned at its inception, particularly in terms of security, but more remained to be done to spur development in Sarawak.
“In terms of security, the communist movement is virtually non-existent now. Our neighbours, Indonesia and the Philippines, have also become part of Asean.
“But when it comes to development, I believe more needs to be done, particularly for Sarawak,” he said.
Commenting on MA63, Linggi said it remains relevant, describing it as the basis for the formation of Malaysia.
“I think the key thing, which is becoming an issue — some say it’s a rather hot issue now — is the implementation of MA63.
“As I said, that is because MA63 is the basis of Malaysia’s formation. And if you recall, those terms (under MA63) were already agreed through the Inter-Governmental Committee Report.
“I know nation-building is not easy. We (Malaysia) are only 63 years old, you look at America (the United States of America)… it is 250 years old and issues still exist among its people. It’s a process,” he said.
Asked what his father would say if he were still alive today, Linggi recalled Jugah’s famous ‘tebu’ principle, which used sugarcane as a metaphor for Malaysia. The analogy, Linggi explained, reflected how sugarcane is sweet at first, but its sweetness can change over time.
“If my father were to come to Sarawak today and ask me, ‘Eh anak, how is our tebu?’, I would say, ‘It is okay. The sweetness is still there, but we require a bit of fertiliser to make it better,’” he said, smiling.
The road ahead
For Linggi, Malaysia Day is not only about remembering how the federation came into being but also about where it is headed.
“Malaysia Day means a lot to me. Let’s say Malaysia is a person. She is 63 years old now. You don’t ask, ‘How were you born?’ Instead, you should ask, ‘How is your life now? How comfortable is your family? What is your plan to have a better life?’ These are the key things we should focus on,” he said.
Linggi, who is the chairman of Tun Jugah Foundation and managing trustee of the Dayak Cultural Foundation, said the fact that Malaysia has remained intact and endured for more than six decades since its formation is something to be proud of.
“Malaysia still exists 63 years later. Why? Because Malaysia, as a person, has a good family.
“We have good ‘parents’, especially in Sarawak. From our early leaders to Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg now, they have looked after us well,” he said.
He believes that Sarawak’s prosperity is closely tied to the strength of Malaysia as a whole, with a stronger Sarawak contributing to a stronger nation.
“Abang Johari’s policy is that he wants to diversify the Sarawak economy so that we can generate better revenue. And once we have better revenue, then Sarawak will be prosperous.
“And if Sarawak prospers, it will strengthen our nation as well. This is how I see it,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s space ambitions start with changing public mindset, says Planetarium Negara director
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Malaysia’s ambitions in the space sector may begin not with rockets or satellites, but with something more fundamental: changing the way Malaysians see and understand space.
Planetarium Negara director Mohd Zamri Shah Mastor said that before Malaysia can build a thriving space economy, it must first build something less tangible — a public that understands, accepts and is ready for it.
“Having a planetarium in the area is important for investors to see.
“They see that if there is a planetarium, it gives them confidence that people there know about space and have at least some knowledge of the sector,” he told
Malay Mail
in a recent interview here.
He recalled how plans for a rocket launch pad in Malaysia had previously faced local opposition, which he attributed in part to a lack of understanding about the concept.
Fast-forward to today, Malaysia is now poised to become South-east Asia’s first country with its own rocket launch pad by 2029, with its location along the Equator offering a distinct advantage by enabling more efficient launches and reducing fuel costs.
Mohd Zamri Shah said this is where Planetarium Negara’s role goes beyond inspiring curiosity, as the presence of planetariums can give potential investors confidence that communities understand and are more likely to embrace space-related projects.
“Investors are very confident when people know about space and they might also find people who can help them expedite their space-related programmes and therefore make the right investment here in Malaysia.
“Even though (our knowledge of the space-related field) it is not very aggressively promoted, they look at the bigger picture, so we have a role to play beyond just creating awareness,” he said.
School students explore the interactive exhibits at Planetarium Negara. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Existing challenge
But achieving that kind of impact comes with its own set of challenges.
“The biggest chunk of our operating expenditure goes towards maintenance. Another major pressure is content development.
“Technology may become cheaper by the day, but developing the content and coming up with ideas is the most expensive part,” Mohd Zamri Shah said, adding that incorporating the necessary technology can drive costs even higher.
When asked whether failing to keep up with evolving technology could leave Planetarium Negara behind, Mohd Zamri Shah agreed but noted the institution must also consider practical challenges such as vandalism when upgrading its exhibits.
“I agree that if we do not upgrade and keep up with the times, there is a risk that the planetarium will be left behind.
“We want to incorporate new technologies into our exhibits, but we also have to consider issues such as vandalism which is very common,” he said, adding that technology-based exhibits can be more easily damaged or worn out compared with older, more robust equipment.
Planetarium Negara director Mohd Zamri Shah Mastor interacts with Nasa’s Eyes on the Solar System, a real-time 3D simulation that allows users to explore the solar system. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
New economy
When asked what success would look like for Planetarium Negara in the future and the impact he hoped it would have on the next generation, Mohd Zamri said the key was “transformation”.
He said success is not merely measured by the number of visitors walking through Planetarium Negara, but by whether their experience changes how they think about space.
“People who come here with a little knowledge about space can become more involved in the field, while those without any knowledge can develop an interest and eventually pursue it.
“That is the core reason why we built a planetarium here.
“Because we found that Malaysia is quite behind in space technology and space exploration,” he said, adding that the decision to build a planetarium was in fact aimed at preparing people’s minds to venture into space.
Despite the cost and challenges, he said the ultimate goal was for the mindset cultivated today to eventually help create a home-grown space industry and a new source of economic growth for Malaysia.
“People may not be selling cars anymore in the future. We want people in Malaysia selling satellites and rockets.
“That is the new economy. We cannot depend on today’s economy forever, so we are preparing for a new one.
“But we hope to change the mindset first, that is our ultimate goal,” he said.

Title: Croatian climber who scaled Mount Kinabalu illegally may face fine
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — The Croatian national who had to be rescued after falling while trying to ascend Mount Kinabalu on an unsanctioned route and without a permit may be slapped with a fine.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said Sabah Parks had lodged a police report over the incident involving the 46-year-old Mauro Persic, who is still in recovery.
“The police and Sabah Parks are investigating the case and looking into what action should be taken. After that, perhaps once he has recovered, we will deal with it,” he told a press conference on the state-level Malaysia Day Celebration here today.
“But considering everything… maybe he will receive a fine,” he added.
Jafry said that the incident should also serve as a lesson to the public not to use unofficial trails to climb Mount Kinabalu, as doing so could pose a safety risk.
Last week, it was reported that a total of 43 search and rescue (SAR) personnel successfully brought Persic down after a five-day operation that also involved challenging terrain and rainy weather conditions.
Persic had attempted to scale the mountain from a separate, closed-off route from Mesilou, but ran into challenges, fell down and had to call authorities for help.
He had initially took part in an extreme adventure race in the Tambatuan area of Kota Belud.
During his ordeal, Persic sustained injuries to his right leg and right ribs, as well as minor wounds to his hands.
The rescue operation involved personnel from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM); the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (STORM) and Mountain Search and Rescue (MOCSAR) team, as well as mountain guides, porters, rangers and other security agencies.
Persic expressed gratefulness to the team who rescued him, especially the porter who carried him down on his back, and said the adventure was “probably not” worth it but thanked the rescue team for the kindness shown to him.

Title: Sabah mulls relocation of Kota Kinabalu central market
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — The Sabah government is mulling three new spots for the relocation of the Kota Kinabalu central market from the heart of the city.
Chief minister Datuk Hajiji Noor who visited and inspected two of the proposed sites – along Likas Bay and near Alamesra, said that no final decision had been made on its suitability or the location of the new market.
The third proposed site is in the area of Darau, some 20km from the city centre.
“The government has plans to relocate this central market from the middle of Kota Kinabalu, so that is why we came to see and inspect the proposed site.
“The government will consider and decide which site is suitable for us to build the new Kota Kinabalu central market,” he told reporters after visiting the site.
Hajiji said the proposed new market was envisaged as more than a conventional public market, with various activities and facilities incorporated into the development like both dry market and wet market, a cultural, local and tourism products centre, hawkers centre and fish wharf.
Hajiji visited a 40-acre piece of state land along Jalan UMS in Alamesra and the second proposed site located on a mixed-commercial land belonging to the Local Government and Housing Ministry near Kampung Likas along Tun Fuad Stephens coastal road adjacent to Anjung Selera.
Hajiji said the Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK) would first prepare a working paper on the proposal before it was brought to the Cabinet for consideration and a decision, saying that the proposal was still in its early stages.
“What is important is that we ensure which site is suitable for building a fairly large and good market, not just an ordinary public market.
“The market to be built will encompass all activities near the market, as we saw at the site earlier. That is the concept,” he said.
Hajiji also said no decision had been made on what would happen to the existing central market site after the relocation.
He said any proposal for the old site would come from the city mayor.
“That proposal will come later from the city mayor on what will be done there. We don't know yet,” he said.
Hajiji also said no cost estimate was available yet, as the government was currently only assessing potential sites.
“The value has not been determined. It is only the site for now,” he said.

Title: Sabah leaders call for apology from Umno man’s remarks on Christianity
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Two Sabah leaders have called on Sepang Umno chief Datuk Noorazli Said to apologise over his controversial remarks concerning christianity and the Bible at the recent Umno general assembly.
Tenom MP Datuk Arthur Kurup said Noorazli’s remarks were “highly inappropriate” and did not reflect the maturity expected of a political leader, while Tuaran MP and Tamparuli assemblyman Datuk Wilfred Madius Tangau described the joke as “grossly inappropriate and offensive”.
Kurup, in a statement, said political differences did not give anyone the licence to make light of another person’s religion and beliefs for the sake of laughter or applause.
“Malaysia was built on the foundations of a multi-racial and multi-religious society. After more than six decades of living together as a nation, it is deeply disappointing that there are still leaders who choose to turn religion into material for political jokes.
“Politics has its limits, freedom of speech comes with responsibility, and religion is not something to be made light of,” he said.
Kurup also reminded political leaders that matters involving the 3Rs — race, religion and the royal institution — should not be touched on indiscriminately.
He said Barisan Nasional, of which Umno is a component party, was founded on principles of unity, stability and solidarity among Malaysians of different races and religions.
“We cannot speak about unity at one moment while, at another, allowing the religion of others to be turned into material for political jokes.
“We must uphold this principle consistently, not only when it benefits us,” said the BN Sabah chairman.
Tangau, meanwhile, called on Noorazli to apologise to the Catholic community over the remarks.
“Sacred Scripture, Catholic priests and religious sisters should not be sexualised or ridiculed from the stage of a major national political party,” Tangau said in a Facebook post.
He also urged Noorazli to acknowledge his “poor judgment”, withdraw the reference to Psalm 129 and offer an “unqualified public apology” to the Catholic and wider Christian community.
The controversy arose after Noorazli made a joke at the Umno general assembly on Saturday involving a priest and a nun, with its punchline attributed to Psalm 129 in the Bible.
However, the purported passage does not appear in Psalm 129.
In a Facebook post following the criticism, Noorazli said the point he was trying to convey through the joke was the importance of focus, perseverance and wisdom in achieving one's goals.
“It was never meant to insult, belittle, or demean anyone or a religion,” he said.
He said the joke was intended as an analogy and that the episode had taught him to be more cautious when using analogies in future.

Title: MACC officer denies key witness against Muhyiddin given ‘special treatment’, ‘immunity’ from own corruption case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) did not give “special treatment” and has not struck a deal with businessman Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff in exchange for him being a key prosecution witness against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, the High Court heard today.
MACC senior assistant commissioner Mazery Mohd Zaini, who investigated Muhyiddin’s power abuse case, confirmed this while testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in the Bersatu president’s trial here.
Under cross-examination by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, Mazery confirmed that Azman was a suspect in an MACC investigation in 2023 involving serious allegations of him and his associated companies KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd soliciting and accepting bribes.
Previously, Azman, who is Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president, confirmed that the two companies had received RM9.35 million from several contractors.
While confirming investigations showed Azman’s companies receiving RM9.35 million from Jana Wibawa contractors, Mazery disagreed that there is a “prima facie” case that Azman had solicited and received bribes.
Mazery said he will not investigate Azman again after this, but said he did not know if the case against Azman has been closed.
Mazery disagreed that his investigation on Azman is “biased”, and also denied protecting Azman.
Hisyam: You protect Datuk Azman because he came to court to give evidence against Tan Sri.
Mazery: I disagree.
Mazery told Hisyam that he did not find it “strange” on the different outcomes for two individuals — where Azman had not been charged for receiving RM1 million from Jana Wibawa contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd while Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad was charged for receiving RM2 million from the same company.
Mazery confirmed that Azman was not remanded during MACC investigations, but denied any special treatment was given to the businessman.
Hisyam: And I say he received special treatment from the MACC because there is a deal between MACC and Azman — testify in court, will be given immunity.
Mazery: I disagree.
Mazery later also disagreed with Hisyam’s suggestion that MACC did not take action on Azman as it needs him to come to court to be a prosecution witness against Muhyiddin.
Hisyam suggested that Azman had no choice but to cooperate with the MACC due to the businessman’s own corruption case, but Mazery disagreed.
Mazery also disagreed that MACC had used the corruption allegations against Azman as a “sword”, also disagreeing that was why Azman had agreed with everything MACC wanted him to agree in court.
Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex on September 2, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
This afternoon, lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin asked why Mazery had disagreed that the RM9.35 million were bribes to Azman.
Mazery then said that his investigations had shown a money trail where those funds were actually meant for the political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
“Because the money that entered Addeen and KCJ’s accounts are actually to be moved to party Bersatu’s account. So it is based on the trail that I made,” he said.
“Based on the money trail I carried out, the money which entered from the companies you mentioned to Addeen and KCJ were re-entered to party Bersatu’s account,” he added.
While confirming that Muhyiddin’s name did not appear in several complaints to the MACC on alleged corruption cases linked to Jana Wibawa and had only appeared in a money laundering complaint, Mazery explained that Muhyiddin was charged because of investigation findings.
“Because based on investigations that were carried out on the complaint, the investigation findings show Datuk Azman asked for donations and deposited them into party Bersatu’s account, as a ‘balasan’ (reward) for Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s helping companies to get Jana Wibawa projects. So because of that, the charges on Tan Sri were carried out,” he explained.
Earlier today, the High Court allowed Muhyiddin’s application to recall four prosecution witnesses on specific issues, saying that this was in the interest of justice.
Muhyiddin’s lawyers had this morning applied to recall those four witnesses, as the prosecution had changed its plans and decided not to call in Adam Radlan as a prosecution witness.
The four witnesses are Azman, contractors Nepturis Sdn Bhd’s Lian Tan Chuan and Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s Shahradzi Shamsuddin, and MACC assistant enforcement officer Mohd Syawaludin Said.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume tomorrow, with Mazery and the four recalled prosecution witnesses expected to take the stand.

Title: Toy-ing with the bomb squad? Suspicious object in Sri Petaling destroyed, found to contain toy blocks (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks after a police bomb disposal unit was called to the scene.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Commissioner Datuk Fadil Marsus said authorities were alerted to the box at about 12.57pm after a 33-year-old woman reported the discovery.
“Initial checks found that the object had a high radiation reading, which prompted the deployment of a Bomb Disposal Unit, together with the Bukit Aman Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosive (CBRNE) Unit, to the scene for further checks and evaluation,” he said.
Representatives from the Malaysian Nuclear Agency were also present.
"The Bomb Disposal Unit then used a Recoilless Disruptor 5.0, an explosive ordnance disposal device, to destroy the suspicious object before discovering several boxes believed to contain colourful building blocks inside the plastic box," he said in a statement here.
He said further checks by the Malaysian Nuclear Agency later confirmed that there were no traces of radioactivity in the vicinity.
Fadil said the case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation.
"The public is also advised not to spread false information that could cause public unrest," he said.
Anyone with information is urged to contact the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-21159999 or the Brickfields police hotline at 03-22979222 or any nearby police stations.
