Title: Ex-director faces 71 cheating charges over RM4.7m used car scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A former director of a used car trading company was charged at three Sessions Courts today with 71 counts of cheating a businessman over the purchase of non-existent used vehicles, resulting in losses of RM4.7 million.
Kee Cher Kian, 34, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out before Judges Azrul Darus, Norma Ismail and Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad.
Before Judge Azrul, Kee faced 26 charges in his capacity as a director of Buycar2u. He was accused of cheating Wong Yoong Jed, a director of Viso Capital Sdn Bhd and Lio Capital Sdn Bhd, by deceiving him into believing that various vehicles had been purchased.
These included the Toyota Alphard and Vellfire, Lexus RX200 and IS 250, Land Rover Evoque, Mini Cooper, Mercedes-Benz C200 and BMW X5.
This induced Wong to transfer RM1.69 million from Lio Capital and Viso Capital into Buycar2u’s bank account.
Before Judges Norma and Muhammad Ilmami, the accused faced 30 charges involving RM1.98 million and 15 charges involving RM1.02 million, respectively.
The offences were allegedly committed at several bank branches around the capital, including at Menara KL Sentral and Jalan Perak, between July 5, 2022 and Aug 3, 2022.
The charges were brought under Section 420 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 10 years and caning, and also liable to a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Siti Suriatey Mohamed Yusoff and Eugenie Meredith Gilbert appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by lawyer J. Matthews.
All three courts allowed the accused to be released on bail of RM215,000 with one surety, along with the additional condition that his passport be surrendered until the case is concluded.
The case mention was fixed for October 16.  — Bernama

Title: Haze update: 22 areas register unhealthy air quality at 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A total of 22 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 4pm today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Serian (181), Sri Aman (166), Samarahan (153) and Kuching (152).
In Johor the air pollutant index for Pasir Gudang was 157, Larkin (156), Pengerang (153), Tangkak (150), Kluang (147) and Kota Tinggi (122).
Other places were Johan Setia (161), Shah Alam (151) and Banting (107) in Selangor; Nilai (155) and Seremban (153) in Negeri Sembilan; Alor Gajah (132) and Bukit Rambai (107) in Melaka; Balok Baru, Kuantan (113) and Indera Mahkota, Kuantan (109) in Pahang; Cheras, Kuala Lumpur (156); Putrajaya (152) and Seri Manjung, Perak (126).
Forty-five areas had a moderate API reading while only Kangar in Perlis had a good API reading.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy and 300 and above, hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Transport minister: Private vehicle ownership transfer inspection fees will remain standardised, no price competition
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — The multi-operator system for motor vehicle inspection services does not allow licensed operators to compete on price, but requires them to focus on the efficiency and quality of their services, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
He said the fee for private vehicle ownership transfer inspections (M.V.15) will remain standardised and regulated by the government through the Road Transport Department (JPJ) at all licensed centres.
“As for the fees, they are set by JPJ and there is a fixed rate. We do not allow inspection centres to charge more than the prescribed rate to protect consumers.
“So, competition cannot be based on lower prices that could undermine the sustainability of industry players. Instead, it should focus on service quality and providing greater convenience and faster service,” he said.
He said this at a press conference held in conjunction with the launch of the M.V.15 Inspection Centre at CARSOME Academy, CARSOME Dealer Hub, here today.
On operational efficiency, Loke said the inspection process at licensed private centres takes less than 20 minutes when conducted according to the prescribed schedule, adding that the results are transmitted directly to the JPJ system, facilitating the vehicle ownership transfer process.
Earlier in his speech, Loke said opening the motor vehicle inspection services market after the single concession expired on Aug 31, 2024, has brought significant benefits to the public by providing a wider choice of services.
He said the opening of the licensed inspection centre by CARSOME Academy marks a milestone, as it is the first M.V.15 centre operated by an automotive Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institution.
“This centre integrates inspection services and technical training under one roof, with inspections carried out by examiners holding a Level 3 Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) in Motor Vehicle Inspection.
“This is in line with the MADANI Government’s agenda to strengthen TVET as a preferred career pathway, while giving students exposure to real-world operations,” he said.
Meanwhile, Loke reminded private operators that their licences came with significant responsibility to ensure legitimate inspection processes and roadworthy vehicles, stressing that the Transport Ministry and JPJ will continue to conduct surprise audits and regular monitoring to safeguard service integrity and standards. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution: Second multi-purpose mission ship under construction in Turkiye to be completed by end‑2027
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The second Multi-Purpose Mission Ship (MPMS), which is currently under construction in Turkiye, is expected to be completed and handed over to the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) by the end of next year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the first MPMS vessel was expected to arrive in March next year, a month before the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA).
“If you recall, two years ago, when President (Recep Tayyip) Erdogan came here, we signed an agreement to purchase one vessel. In less than two years, it is now ready.
“Compared with (if) we were to build it ourselves, there have been various cases where vessels were not completed, funds were exhausted and all sorts of other issues. This has given the Home Ministry confidence that it made the right decision, with a shorter construction period and a reasonable price,” he told the media after attending the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said he would travel to Istanbul, Turkiye, at the end of this month to personally inspect the progress of the vessel’s construction.
He said the vessel’s construction was progressing ahead of schedule, further convincing the ministry that its decision was the right one in terms of the construction period and reasonable price.
The development of the vessel is another important step in efforts to strengthen the capabilities of the MMEA, particularly in addressing an increasingly complex maritime security environment.
In a related development, the ministry will evaluate an offer for a second offshore patrol vessel previously operated by the United States Coast Guard (USCG), based on its seaworthiness and repair costs.
Saifuddin Nasution said the evaluation would be based on a report by Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman following an inspection conducted with MMEA experts, engineers and officers.
“They made the offer, but we have to satisfy ourselves (as to whether) it is seaworthy or not. So I tasked the secretary-general to go and inspect it, then submit a report to me,” he said.
He said Malaysia had previously received its first offshore patrol vessel from the USCG, which is now stationed in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah.
He added that cooperation with the USCG had been established since the formation of the MMEA and covered areas such as asset contributions, training, joint operations and intelligence sharing.
“If its seaworthiness is low and the cost to us is even higher, that would be a burden. We will not agree to it,” he said.
The government previously acquired the KM BENDAHARA offshore patrol vessel through the United States Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programme, and it was officially handed over to the MMEA on Sept 5, 2025, in Baltimore, United States. — Bernama

Title: Carried by teenager porter, rescued Croatian climber says Kinabalu ordeal broke his heart
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Croatian climber Mauro Persic has expressed regret over the risks he took after being found injured and alone on Mount Kinabalu for eight days, but said the ordeal strengthened his faith in human compassion.
Persic, 46, said the rescue operation was a humbling experience, particularly when rescuers and porters had to carry him down because he was too weak and injured to continue on his own,
Berita Harian
reported.
One of the moments that struck him most was being carried by a porter estimated to be about 15 years old.
“One of the porters was so young, perhaps 15 years (old), I could feel each impact of his legs and knees, it broke my heart that I'm contributing to this
“Was it all worth it? I don’t know. Probably not. Broken body. 40 people risking their lives to save one. But still, I’ve seen the very best of humanity showing up these days; generosity, kindness and care,” he wrote in a Facebook post.
He added that rescuers brought him food, chocolate and snacks, gathered around campfires, shared jokes and kept him company while efforts were made to bring him down safely.
The Croatian climber, who was rescued last week in an operation involving multiple agencies, sustained injuries to his right leg and ribs, as well as minor wounds to his hands during the incident.

Title: Anthony Loke calls for Pakatan Presidential Council meeting to discuss recent political developments after Umno assembly
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he will propose to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council convene to discuss recent political developments following statements made at the Umno General Assembly.
He said the recent statements raised concerns regarding political certainty and stability, which could affect investor and public confidence in the country.
Loke said the developments were viewed with concern and serious consideration, adding that he would request Anwar, who is PH chairman, to call for a Presidential Council meeting to review and discuss the latest developments upon his return from his overseas trip.
“Some of the statements made are of course not good in terms of political certainty and political stability in the country, as component parties in the government seem to not be heading in the same direction.
“So this is something which would not give much confidence to investors and to the public. The Prime Minister must also make this clear with all component parties,” the Transport Minister said.
Loke said this when met by reporters after officiating the CARSOME Academy M.V.15 Vehicle Inspection Centre at the CARSOME Dealer Hub here.
He was responding to media queries on remarks made by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in his winding-up speech at the recently concluded Umno assembly, which touched on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) position in the Unity Government.
On whether PH would seek clarification on BN’s position or the challenges issued by the Umno leadership, Loke maintained that any official top-level response should come directly from the Prime Minister. — Bernama

Title: Penang Port Commission, PPSB to offer free ferry services on Malaysia Day
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Penang Port Commission (SPPP) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) are offering free ferry services to Malaysians on September 16 in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations and the Keretapi Sarong Festival.
SPPP chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the offer applies to trips from both ferry terminals, Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Seberang Perai and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) here, in accordance with the existing service schedule.
“With this free ferry service offer, I hope to alleviate the financial burden on Malaysians while providing an opportunity to celebrate Malaysia Day and participate in the Keretapi Sarong Festival in a meaningful way,” he said in a statement today.
He noted that commuters would enjoy savings of RM2 per one-way trip for pedestrians and RM2.50 for two-wheeled vehicle users.
According to him, during last year’s Malaysia Day celebration, a total of 10,094 pedestrians and 1,909 two-wheeled vehicles utilised the ferry service for round trips.
Yeoh added that these figures contributed to the overall annual total of 3,131,131 pedestrians and 784,065 two-wheeled vehicles recorded in 2025.
He said the initiative also aims to help reduce traffic congestion in Penang, in addition to encouraging the use of more sustainable and efficient public transportation. — Bernama

Title: Chief of Defence Force: MAF proposes reinstating multi‑agency border‑security framework used under former national task force
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) has submitted a proposal to the National Security Council (NSC) to reinstate a multi-agency operational framework modelled on the National Task Force (NTF) to bolster national border security.
Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the proposal, submitted through the National Operational Management Committee, would bring together various agencies including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM), and the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM).
He said the strategic coordination of enforcement agencies has proven more effective in addressing security vulnerabilities along the country’s land and maritime borders.
“We executed this (integrated operation) previously via the NTF during the Covid-19 pandemic, and it proved effective in coordinating multi-agency efforts before the mechanism was changed for specific reasons.
“Therefore, I believe elements of that approach should be reinstated, even if not on a large scale, to address current security challenges and vulnerabilities,” he said during a Special Media Interview with the Chief of Defence Forces in conjunction with the 93rd MAF Day at Wisma Pertahanan here today.
Malek Razak said the MAF conducts round-the-clock surveillance along the national border and regularly detains intruders, though not all cases are reported to the media.
“Malaysia also maintains close cooperation with neighbouring countries such as Thailand and Indonesia to tackle cross-border security issues through intelligence sharing,” he explained.
Touching on integrity issues, he said the main measure against corruption at the border is instilling integrity and high moral values among personnel.
The NTF, was established to carry out Op Benteng to curb the influx of illegal immigrants during the pandemic in 2020, was officially disbanded on December 31, 2022. — Bernama

Title: Two‑year‑old mauled by stray dogs in Batu Pahat to undergo reconstructive surgery
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Sept 14 — A two-year-old girl mauled by stray dogs outside her grandmother’s home in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, is expected to undergo reconstructive surgery soon as she continues to fight for her life.
Nur Haira Wafiqah Mohammad Hamizi was critically injured in the Sept 6 attack by five dogs, suffering severe head and facial wounds.
As reported by
Berita Harian
, Haira’s aunt, who wished to be identified only as Nur, 23, said doctors had informed the child’s parents that reconstructive surgery was the best option given the extent of her injuries.
“We were told that ordinary treatment or surgery would not be suitable. Haira can now breathe on her own without respiratory support. She has also opened her eyes, though there is no response yet. The medical team is still monitoring her condition, and we ask everyone to pray for her recovery,” she said.
Nur also told
BH
that before all the dogs involved in the attack could be captured, villagers in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, were confronted by another pack of strays.
She said around 10 dogs were spotted in an oil palm plantation behind the victim’s grandfather’s house, and their presence was even recorded on video before they disappeared.
“I believe 10 other dogs appeared at the plantation around 11am today. Previously, the authorities caught seven dogs, including five puppies, which attacked Haira. Three more have yet to be captured and are still roaming near the house.
“Now another pack of strays has emerged, raising fears they could cause further problems and disturb residents. We do not want a repeat of what happened to my niece,” she said.

Title: Free entry to three Penang heritage sites for two days starting tomorrow in conjunction with Malaysia Day
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — Three heritage sites in Penang will offer free entry for two days from tomorrow in conjunction with the fifth anniversary of Penang Hill’s recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve and Malaysia Day.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the three sites are the Penang State Automotive Gallery, Fort Cornwallis and the Penang State Museum.
“The public and tourists from Malaysia and abroad, are welcome to take this opportunity to explore history, appreciate the state’s heritage, gain a deeper understanding of Penang’s past and discover Malaysia’s rich and diverse cultural heritage,” he said in a statement today.
He said free admission to the Automotive Gallery and Fort Cornwallis had also been extended until October, giving the public more time to visit the two sites. — Bernama

Title: Federal Court hears PKR’s argument that Zuraida’s RM10m bond was reasonable; decision reserved
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Federal Court was told today that the High Court’s decision ordering former Ampang MP Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin to pay RM10 million to Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) for breaching a bond with the party was reasonable.
PKR counsel Ranjit Singh submitted that there was an admission of fact that RM10 million, or a sum exceeding that amount, had been expended on Zuraida.
“Zuraida admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the operative clause fixed RM10 million as the sum payable upon the occurrence of the stipulated events,” he said during PKR’s appeal against a Court of Appeal decision reducing the bond payment from RM10 million to RM100,000.
Ranjit submitted that the appeal ultimately turned on the legal consequence of a contractual admission of value where Section 75 of the Contracts Act is invoked.
“The recital recorded Zuraida’s admission that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million. Section 75 remains the statutory control against penal, oppressive or unconscionable stipulations. But it must be applied to the contract as it stands, including the facts contractually admitted by the parties,” he said.
The counsel submitted that although the bond was contractual in nature, it had been executed against the backdrop of the country’s political landscape at the time, when political coalitions were prevalent, and party-hopping had become a scourge, amid concerns that it could lead to the collapse of governments.
“One must read the bond in a manner that explains why the sum of RM10 million was stipulated, which at first glance may appear excessive. But the reality is, look at what happened. The Sheraton Move led to the collapse of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition at the Federal level,” he said. He was assisted by lawyer Navpreet Singh.
Meanwhile, Zuraida’s counsel Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun contended that there was no separate or special category of “political contract” that stood exempt from Section 75 of the Contracts Act.
“The party cannot use its status and position as a political party to bypass statutory protections against penalty clauses. Section 75 of the Act does not cease to apply merely because the contractual obligations arose in the context of a political party.
“To hold otherwise would create, by judicial implication, an exception to Section 75. This court should not countenance such an approach,” said Azhar Azizan, who was assisted by counsel Nizamuddin Hamid.
Azhar said the relationship between a political party and its candidate was, in practical terms, institutional in nature. The individual candidate lacked equal legal bargaining power when negotiating the quantum of a unilateral bond imposed as the condition or price of candidacy.
“This unequal bargaining power is not dependent on the candidate’s seniority or position in the party. The bond demonstrates that it was not an individually negotiated agreement in which the respondent freely negotiated and agreed that RM10 million represented a reasonable measure of compensation in the event of default.
“It was imposed on the respondent by the party,” he said, adding that the RM100,000 imposed by the Court of Appeal was reasonable.
After hearing submissions from both parties, the three-member bench, chaired by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh and comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin, reserved its decision for a date to be scheduled later.
On June 24, 2025, the Federal Court granted PKR leave to appeal the matter.
This followed the Court of Appeal’s decision on December 11, 2024, when a three-member panel upheld the High Court’s finding that Zuraida had breached the bond, but reduced the quantum payable from RM10 million to RM100,000.
The Court of Appeal’s ruling came after the High Court in Kuala Lumpur, on June 23, 2023, ruled in favour of PKR and ordered Zuraida to pay RM10 million in accordance with the bond’s terms. The presiding judge, Datuk Akhtar Tahir, held that the bond was a valid and binding contract.
The lawsuit had been initiated in 2020 by PKR secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail on behalf of the party, claiming that Zuraida had violated the terms of a bond she signed before contesting in the 14th General Election in 2018.
Under the bond, Zuraida, a former Housing and Local Government Minister, was required to pay PKR RM10 million within seven days if she resigned from the party, joined another political party, or became an independent representative after being elected on the party’s ticket. — Bernama

Title: New Lawas Hospital expected to evolve into specialist centre to cut long‑distance referrals, says deputy health minister
Article:
LAWAS, Sept 14 — The new 76-bed Lawas Hospital is expected to evolve into a specialist hospital, thereby reducing the local population’s reliance on distant hospitals.
Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib stated that current manpower constraints have resulted in incomplete staffing at the hospital, a situation that will improve once additional personnel are secured.
“I hope that God willing, medical specialists will be permanently based at Lawas Hospital, rather than relying on scheduled visiting specialists.
“It has been difficult for the people to access specialist care, as they previously had to be sent to distant hospitals. I hope this facility will become a specialist hospital,” she said at the Lawas Hospital project handover ceremony here today.
The new hospital is equipped with, among other facilities, two operating theatres, a patient kitchen, an ICT lab enabling remote consultations with medical specialists, nine haemodialysis machines, and 76 beds, including four beds in the High Dependency Ward.
Hanifah noted that geographical factors make comprehensive health facilities in Lawas crucial; previously, patients requiring specialist referrals had to travel approximately one and a half hours to Limbang and about three and a half hours to Miri via certain routes.
Meanwhile, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi, who also attended the ceremony, stated that the RM183 million Lawas Hospital project was built by the Public Works Department’s Special Project Team 2 starting June 30, 2020, using a Design and Build method undertaken by MCS Management Sdn Bhd.
He expressed hope that the hospital would improve community access to quality healthcare services and serve as a catalyst for enhancing the quality of healthcare service delivery in Lawas. — Bernama

Title: Abdul Aziz appointed Deputy Inspector‑General of Police
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Management Director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid has been appointed Deputy Inspector-General of Police, effective September 9.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the appointment was consented to by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and upon the recommendation of the Police Force Commission, in accordance with Clauses 4 and 5 of Article 140 of the Federal Constitution.
“Abdul Aziz’s expertise and experience in policing, coupled with his strong leadership and competence, make him well suited to serve as Deputy Inspector-General of Police.
“The government congratulates him on his appointment,” he said in a statement today.
Abdul Aziz, 59, was born in Penaga, Penang, on February 19, 1967, and holds a Master of Social Sciences (Police Studies) from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM).
He joined the PDRM on July 1, 1995, and has served in various departments throughout his career, including the Management Department, Special Branch, Criminal Investigation Department, Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, Commercial Crime Investigation Department, Logistics and Technology Department, and Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department.
Abdul Aziz has held several key positions, including Management Director, Deputy Director of Special Branch, Deputy Director of Narcotics, Penang Police Deputy Chief, Principal Assistant Director of Management Policy/Human Resource, and Principal Assistant Director of the Special Integrated Investigation Team.
He has also attended various international courses and seminars, including the 8th International Symposium of Best Police Practice in Dubai, and the Intelligence Management Development Programme in Australia. — Bernama

Title: Sixteen drownings in Pahang this year, Bomba urges public to respect warning signs
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 14 — A total of 16 drowning deaths have been recorded in Pahang so far this year, and the public is urged to prioritise safety when engaging in activities near rivers, waterfalls, and beaches.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations and rescue, Mohd Salahuddin Isa, said key safety measures include heeding warning signs and refraining from swimming in areas identified as dangerous.
He added that visitors must also be vigilant regarding the “water surge” phenomenon particularly when at waterfalls, rapids, and rivers.
“To date, 16 drowning cases resulting in 16 deaths have been recorded across the state; we advise the public to always prioritise safety and understand the risks associated with recreational areas.
“Never swim in areas marked with red flags or ‘No Swimming’ warning signs,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Salahuddin advised that if a person appears to be drowning, members of the public should not immediately jump into the water unless they possess rescue skills.
Instead, assistance can be provided using the ‘Reach, Throw, Row, Go’ concept: trying to reach the victim with a long object like a stick or pole (Reach), throwing a floating object such as a lifebuoy (Throw), using a boat if available (Row), or calling the 999 emergency line to dispatch the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) to the location (Go). — Bernama
